docs.title: 1 Introduction
docs.text:
This document is part of APTITUDE horizontal interoperability RFC for credential issuance.

It establishes the baseline, cross-pilot profile to be used by APTITUDE pilots and technical implementations for the issuance of 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:0594ee68147b2b331d57c1ad5cba0271: in a consistent and testable manner.

This RFC profiles issuance based on:

  • OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance (OpenID4VCI) 1.0
  • OpenID4VC High Assurance Interoperability Profile (HAIP) 1.0
  • ETSI TS 119 472-3

against the ARF and CIR snapshot defined in Section 1.1.

The purpose of this document is to provide:

  • a stable starting point for interoperability across APTITUDE pilots;
  • a common baseline for Wallets, Issuers, and 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:1cc4c93983bd42a88966806fea791d4d:;
  • a requirements set that can be translated into ITB+ conformance test suites;
  • a basis for pilot-specific issuance profiles that need stricter domain or credential-format constraints.

    • This specification focuses only on issuance. It covers wallet-initiated and issuer-initiated issuance, including both Authorisation Code Flow and Pre-Authorised Code Flow, together with the metadata, security bindings, and proof mechanisms needed to support interoperable issuance.

    This document does not define presentation or verifier behavior as such. Pilot-specific or Trust-Framework profiles MAY define additional issuance-side policy metadata.

docs.title: 1.1 Reference baseline
docs.text:
For D2.1, this RFC uses the following architectural and legal snapshot. Later ARF or CIR revisions are out of scope unless a subsequent RFC revision explicitly updates this baseline.

  • ARF v3.0.0 (2026-07-21) is the Architecture and Reference Framework reference, in particular Annex 2 Topic 10 (Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit). Subsequent mentions of “the ARF” in this RFC mean ARF v3.0.0.
  • CIR (EU) 2024/2982 (protocols and interfaces), as amended by CIR (EU) 2026/1731, is the issuance-protocol CIR. The applicable provisions are Article 4 and Annex I, which designate ETSI TS 119 472-3 V1.1.1 for issuance of PID and electronic attestations of attributes.
  • CIR (EU) 2024/2979 (integrity and core functionalities), as amended by CIR (EU) 2026/1731, is the Wallet Unit Attestation CIR. The applicable provisions are Article 6 and Annex Ib (Wallet Instance Attestation and Key Attestation).
  • CIR (EU) 2024/2977 (PID and EAA), as amended by CIR (EU) 2026/1731, applies where issuance-side PID or EAA constraints are relevant.

In the remainder of this RFC, the short forms CIR 2024/2982, CIR 2024/2979, and CIR 2024/2977 mean those acts as amended by CIR (EU) 2026/1731. Generic “CIR” references without an identifier are not used.

docs.title: 2 Scope
docs.text:
This specification defines:

  • a baseline profile of OpenID4VCI for issuing 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c0f578b2b5f55e3909b811ad6897817a:;
  • requirements for Wallets that request, receive, validate, and store credentials;
  • requirements for 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c12344af706185c0209cbdc819f2efb6: and their 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c5aedd03bcc430f4d559c6698af8e554:;
  • support for wallet-initiated issuance and issuer-initiated issuance via 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:3f1f4e2fff8e9b5ae59062caf717800d:<__None__>;
  • support for both Authorisation Code Flow and Pre-Authorised Code Flow;
  • the minimum endpoints, metadata, and request-processing rules necessary to enable interoperable issuance;
  • issuance-side requirements for wallet attestation, 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:88e38ff528cdad05d207e991140cb4c0:, 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:528f7c4eb5c402a3425efa63af5ab173:, and deferred issuance;
  • conditional notification handling where the selected deployment supports issuance notifications;

    • This document is intentionally horizontal and cross-pilot. It does not define credential-specific claim sets, domain schemas, or sector-specific assurance rules, except where a specific issuance profile requires explicit protocol-level constraints.

    This document describes:

    • issuance protocol flows;
    • baseline security and privacy requirements;
    • interfaces and endpoints, including Wallet invocation, 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:17ae3b51d07f86d33d03e78eb8015b2e:<__None__>, PAR, Token, Credential, Deferred Credential, 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:4435adf103285f2b16b14051c18db908:<__None__>, Notification, and metadata endpoints where applicable;
    • conformance requirements that can be mapped to ITB+ test cases.

docs.title: 2.1 Out of Scope
docs.text:
The following are out of scope for this RFC:

  • presentation and verification flows;
  • verifier requirements;
  • trust framework governance, federation policy, and trust-list operations, except where issuance processing requires validation against such trust material;
  • credential-specific semantic profiles and domain-specific claim definitions;
  • pilot-specific UX constraints;
  • business, legal, or organisational policy beyond the protocol-visible issuance requirements captured in metadata;
  • credential reuse policy, disclosure policy, and enforcement of such policies, except for protocol elements explicitly defined by another referenced APTITUDE or Trust Framework profile.

docs.title: 3 Normative Language
docs.text: The key words SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, MAY, and OPTIONAL in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.

docs.title: 4 Roles and Components
docs.text:
This specification uses the following roles:

  • Wallet Unit / Wallet: The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a24cf291828384debbf7d2b785cc52db:<__None__>, as defined in ARF v3.0.0 and the APTITUDE glossary, including its 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:081ad4489cf52334b00a0ad0002ed7a0:, acting on behalf of the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:4a8c3191a393b08ca4f5a6c688e5c69f:<__None__> to request, receive, validate, store, and manage 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:d65427bd8137b9f876d26e12eb40ff88: and associated cryptographic material. Where the distinction between Wallet Unit and Wallet Instance is not material, this RFC uses the short term Wallet.
  • 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:84183b95e3d678802d0890cdc6c1840b:<__None__>: As defined in the APTITUDE glossary: the natural person or legal representative controlling the Wallet and authorising credential issuance or presentation.
  • 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:d3150ce9effc2f55362a8ea9bb39e126: (AP): As defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with ARF v3.0.0: the entity that decides to issue 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:abd8ce1571474d3ea1b550f74d3c44be: and operates, or is associated with, the issuance service.
  • 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:6cf2209793a1a8e79a54e7532091f816: (AS): As defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with ARF v3.0.0: the OAuth 2.0 / OpenID component responsible for authenticating the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:9bfcc710643d9a8b4d1f58a84a443c6a:<__None__> and issuing tokens authorising access to the Credential and related endpoints.

    The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:89ee40994b276661aa11ae6526ad9ccc: MAY be co-located with the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a2769e38de6cda4a63f24258042a53fb: or MAY be operated separately.

docs.title: 5 Protocol Overview
docs.text:
The APTITUDE issuance baseline is based on OpenID4VCI 1.0, constrained by HAIP 1.0, and aligned with the issuance-protocol requirements selected from ETSI TS 119 472-3. The ETSI-aligned requirements stated in this RFC are mandatory baseline requirements; ETSI reuse and disclosure-policy requirements remain outside this RFC's scope.

The profile adopts the following baseline choices:

WIA, DPoP, and KA are separate protocol concepts. WIA authenticates the Wallet Instance as an OAuth client; DPoP sender-constrains OAuth requests and access tokens; and KA attests credential-binding key material at the Credential Endpoint. In this RFC, KA means the OpenID4VCI key-attestation object; for the ETSI-aligned baseline, it is the WUA profile of that object defined by ETSI TS 119 472-3.

Where WIA authentication and DPoP are both required for the same request, APTITUDE uses the combined mode defined in draft-ietf-oauth-attestation-based-client-auth-11. The request uses the attest_jwt_client_auth_dpop Token Endpoint authentication method and carries OAuth-Client-Attestation: <WIA> and DPoP: <proof signed with the private key corresponding to WIA.cnf>. The DPoP proof performs both the RFC 9449 sender-constraining function and the proof-of-possession function required for WIA-based client authentication; a separate Client Attestation PoP JWT is not required. The AS and Resource Server MAY independently issue DPoP-Nonce values. Authorization Server Metadata SHALL advertise attest_jwt_client_auth_dpop as a supported Token Endpoint authentication method and dpop_combined in client_attestation_pop_methods_supported.

  • support for Authorisation Code Flow for issuance interactions requiring 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:0e424740bc49caaa8b5200d6c3e230fd:<__None__> authentication and authorisation;
  • support for Pre-Authorised Code Flow for issuer-initiated issuance scenarios where issuance is initiated through a 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:25698eaf6628cfe1b501baf22baf3532:<__None__> and the applicable grant is pre-authorised;
  • support for issuer-initiated issuance via 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:22c3bb41fab0813c648080692c3283bb:<__None__>;
  • support for wallet-initiated issuance, where the Wallet selects a credential type or credential configuration and derives the corresponding request parameters from Issuer metadata;
  • use of Pushed Authorisation Requests (PAR) for Authorisation Code Flow requests under this profile;
  • use of 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:2b91d8f31841dc777002a708bc617429:<__None__> with S256 for Authorisation Code Flow;
  • use of 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:d9a56f80f866d5a14a2791212718ec8b:<__None__> as defined in RFC 9449 for sender-constraining access tokens and applicable HTTP requests;
  • use of 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a0bef18a40f0aea2be4f8abf101dad1d:<__None__> as OAuth client authentication material at the PAR and Token endpoints;
  • support for 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:150bce633f34c82f3b7db2181b0755d8: / 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:d8d4e71ea6c6e634357a36c6b2b62468: during credential issuance;
  • support for Key Attestation (KA) and proofs structures at the Credential Endpoint for device-bound issuance;
  • support for deferred issuance where immediate issuance is not possible;
  • support for issuance-side metadata defined by applicable APTITUDE or Trust-Framework profiles.

    • Wallets and Issuers SHALL support the A128GCM and A256GCM algorithms, in addition to the cryptographic suites required by OpenID4VC-HAIP.

    The following ETSI-aligned issuance requirements apply:

    • same-device Wallet invocation SHALL support the custom URL scheme eu-eaa-offer://;
    • Issuer Metadata SHALL be signed metadata as defined by OpenID4VCI, and the JWS protected header SHALL carry the Issuer access certificate in x5c as profiled by ETSI;
    • Issuer Metadata SHALL support the issuer_info metadata parameter to transport issuer registration material, including the registration certificate and registrar-provided registration information, as profiled by ETSI.

    Providers shall support at least one of authorization_code or urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:040e472e52930df827ac6d763a0945ad:<__None__>. This RFC profiles both, and treats them as first-class issuance paths. PAR requirements apply only to the Authorisation Code Flow path.

    For Authorisation Code Flow, this profile assumes the Wallet interacts with the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:5e65000357cecea6b77976efdceee375: using PAR, receives an authorisation code, exchanges it at the Token Endpoint, and then calls the Credential Endpoint. 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:1adea1a587d073dbf121e2125e591913: is carried at both the PAR and Token endpoints, together with DPoP proof signed by the key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b7f1b2f41cbb1c4ac87caee823b9e621: cnf claim.

    For device-bound issuance, ETSI requires the Credential Request to carry a proofs parameter containing either jwt or attestation. In the jwt mechanism, the Wallet proves possession of a key to be bound to the credential and carries the Key Attestation (KA) in the key_attestation protected header parameter. In the attestation mechanism, the Wallet carries the KA directly without separate proof of possession of each attested key. The Issuer's processing rules differ accordingly and are profiled in the normative sections below.

docs.title: 5.1 Credential Format Baseline
docs.text:
This RFC defines the interoperability baseline at protocol level for the following formats only:

  • SD-JWT VC;
  • ISO mdoc.

Other credential formats, including JSON-LD variants and X.509-AC EAA, are outside this RFC unless another APTITUDE profile explicitly defines them. ETSI credential-format terminology used by such profiles is defined in ETSI TS 119 472-1.

To preserve a stable horizontal baseline, pilot-specific RFCs SHALL specify any additional constraints for a concrete credential format and SHALL NOT relax the mandatory requirements in this document.

docs.title: 5.2 Pilot-specific extensions
docs.text:
Pilot-specific issuance RFCs MAY extend this profile with:

  • concrete credential configuration identifiers;
  • claim set and schema rules;
  • assurance-level requirements;
  • format-specific proof rules;
  • issuance policy constraints.

Such extensions SHALL remain compatible with this baseline.

docs.title: 6 High-level Flows
docs.text:
This section describes the high-level issuance interactions supported by this RFC.

This profile supports:

  • wallet-initiated issuance;
  • issuer-initiated issuance via 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:70c0026baa988e62b6410919ce033650:<__None__>;
  • Authorisation Code Flow;
  • Pre-Authorised Code Flow;
  • immediate issuance and deferred issuance.

For issuance interactions using the Authorisation Code Flow, the Wallet uses PAR before user authorisation. The Wallet sends 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:134f0639defbecb171b38fa7a0f2c505:<__None__> to the PAR Endpoint and again to the Token Endpoint, with DPoP proof signed by the key referenced by the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:5df3593adf1d4b1666c80bf2c13ddefe: cnf claim.

For issuance interactions using the Pre-Authorised Code Flow, no PAR or authorisation redirect is required. The Wallet processes the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:fb96a35b34bdd9aecbb8ab884a314748:<__None__>, redeems the pre-authorised grant at the Token Endpoint, and proceeds to the Credential Endpoint.

For PID issuance under the ETSI-aligned baseline, Pre-Authorised Code Flow user authorisation SHALL use physical presence. An APTITUDE profile requiring a high level of assurance for online PID issuance SHALL NOT use Pre-Authorised Code Flow.

For device-bound issuance, the Wallet sends a Credential Request containing a proofs structure as profiled by this RFC. The Credential Request carries Key Attestation (KA) at the Credential Endpoint, either in the protected header of proofs.jwt[*] or directly in proofs.attestation[*], depending on the mechanism used.

Because this RFC is issuance-only, presentation and verifier behavior are not described here except where issuer-provided issuance metadata is needed by the Wallet for later use.

docs.title: 6.1.1 Configuration and discovery
docs.text:
1. Before initiating issuance, the Wallet SHALL obtain or use a valid cached copy of Credential Issuer Metadata and the applicable Authorization Server Metadata. The Wallet obtains Credential Issuer Metadata, including at minimum:
    • 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:720a472d6ee896d0e0e4c41c9c86d2f5: metadata;
    • supported credential configurations;
    • the mapping between offered credential configurations and the request parameters needed to initiate issuance;
    • supported grant types;
    • supported proof methods and the OpenID4VCI c_nonce retrieval mechanism;
    • The Wallet determines the Authorization Server identifier from Credential Issuer Metadata. If authorization_servers is present, the Wallet uses the selected grant's authorization_server hint only when the array contains multiple Authorization Server identifiers. The hint value MUST match an entry in the authorization_servers array; if it is present when the array does not contain multiple entries, or does not match an entry, the Wallet SHALL treat the Credential Offer as invalid. If no valid hint is present, the Wallet selects the applicable Authorization Server from the array. If authorization_servers is absent, it uses the Credential Issuer identifier as the Authorization Server issuer identifier. The Wallet obtains the corresponding Authorization Server Metadata and uses it to discover the Token Endpoint, PAR Endpoint, supported DPoP signing algorithms, including dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, and combined-attestation support.
    • The Wallet retrieves and processes signed Issuer Metadata carrying: - the Issuer access certificate in the JWS x5c protected header; and - the issuer_info metadata parameter for issuer registration material.
    • If no valid cached metadata exists, or if endpoints or advertised capabilities have changed, the Wallet refreshes the relevant metadata before continuing. The Wallet determines whether the selected issuance interaction is supported through:
      • Authorisation Code Flow;
      • Pre-Authorised Code Flow; or
      • both.

docs.title: 6.1.2 User selects credential
docs.text:
1. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c8336e39f430af7d32cde58f42630ae3:<__None__> chooses a credential type or credential configuration.
  2. The Wallet identifies the corresponding credential configuration and the applicable issuance path.
  3. Where the selected issuance path is wallet-initiated Authorisation Code Flow, the Wallet prepares an authorisation request as defined below.

docs.title: 6.1.3 Pushed Authorisation Request (PAR)
docs.text:
1. For wallet-initiated Authorisation Code Flow, the Wallet constructs an authorisation request containing at minimum: - client_id; - the relevant scope, authorization_details, or other profiled authorisation parameters; - code_challenge using 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:d97eab5c6cb8e79f6b20601764b217ab:<__None__> S256; - redirect_uri; - response_type=code; - state; - the required credential-related authorisation parameters.
  2. The Wallet sends the request to the Issuer's PAR Endpoint.
  3. The Wallet includes: - the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b5d9fe696d93f5ce9932cf4b44b4a61e: at the PAR request; and - a DPoP proof signed by the key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:729d011df3dc7e35f4579fd8e5283601: cnf claim.
  4. The PAR Endpoint validates the request and returns a request_uri and validity information.

docs.title: 6.1.4 User authorisation
docs.text:
1. The Wallet directs the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:6f884f3f8c7cfe5262af07b1604ce96e:<__None__> to the Authorisation Endpoint using the request_uri obtained from PAR.
  2. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:06593a06f86a9a63458c554ddb3afdcd:<__None__> authenticates according to the Issuer's policy.
  3. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:f0f2676c72486e7d4845db58c770c4a1:<__None__> authorises the issuance transaction.
  4. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:8ef7a2129940b1f675a1bfe1d90b9852: redirects back to the Wallet with an authorisation code and state.

docs.title: 6.1.5 Token request
docs.text:
1. The Wallet sends a token request to the Token Endpoint, including: - grant_type=authorization_code; - code; - redirect_uri; - code_verifier; - WIA-based client authentication and a DPoP proof.
  2. The Wallet includes: - the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:4c53712c3dc6517688f194255a35fb86: at the Token Endpoint; and - a DPoP proof signed by the key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:ea7743f8c4c2372e3cc92c4fb746b443: cnf claim.
  3. The Token Endpoint validates the request and returns: - a sender-constrained access_token; - optional refresh_token or other explicitly defined OAuth/OpenID4VCI parameters; - an optional DPoP-Nonce HTTP response header.

docs.title: 6.1.6 Credential request
docs.text:
1. After receiving the Token response and immediately before generating credential proof material, the Wallet obtains a fresh OpenID4VCI c_nonce from the Issuer's 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:0bb25452a096625019111826cecbc1b4:<__None__> Endpoint.
  2. The Wallet sends a request to the Credential Endpoint containing: - Authorization: DPoP {access_token}; - a DPoP proof bound to the access-token key; - the requested credential configuration or other format-specific request parameters; - a proofs structure or equivalent proof material, according to the selected proof mechanism.
  3. For device-bound issuance, the request SHALL include issuance proof material that binds the issued credential to Wallet-controlled key material.
  4. Where the selected proof method is based on proofs.jwt: - the Wallet proves possession of the private key to be bound to the credential; and - the Wallet carries the Key Attestation (KA) in the protected header parameter profiled for key attestation.
  5. Where the selected proof method is based on proofs.attestation: - the Wallet carries the Key Attestation (KA) directly in the attestation structure; and - the Issuer processes the request according to the rules applicable to attested keys under the selected profile.
  6. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c5c89e79b046a8e61d2fee0c890f82fe: validates: - the access token and its sender-constraining mechanism; - the credential request syntax; - the OpenID4VCI c_nonce and proof material; - the applicable wallet attestation material; - applicable issuance policy defined by another referenced profile; - any credential-specific prerequisites.
  7. The Issuer returns the credential immediately, or signals deferred issuance.

docs.title: 6.1.7 Storage
docs.text:
1. The Wallet validates the returned credential and associated metadata.
  2. The Wallet stores the credential under 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:88a717497e2fab677e0d078343b871a8:<__None__> control.
  3. The Wallet stores issuer-provided metadata required by this RFC or another referenced APTITUDE or Trust-Framework profile.

docs.title: 6.2 Issuer-initiated Issuance via Credential Offer
docs.text:
In the issuer-initiated flow, the Issuer first decides to issue and then provides a 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:78a087bf73d1ec2b406589f231cb89c8:<__None__> that the Wallet uses to continue the issuance process.

Actors: 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:14a1d990358f61fa9c39557ce6a69c85:<__None__>, Wallet, Issuer, optionally 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:6c5c8d9f8621c26848829f3062007a04:.

docs.title: 6.2.1 Issuance decision
docs.text:
1. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:324d47f467cc508970add3512027d6c2:<__None__> interacts with the Issuer in a business process such as onboarding, enrolment, registration, or completion of an eligibility step.
  2. Following successful checks, the Issuer decides to issue one or more credentials.

docs.title: 6.2.2 Credential Offer creation
docs.text:
1. The Issuer constructs a 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:60451b8d3416b3b89737b742a32b4b26:<__None__> that includes at minimum: - the credential_issuer identifier; - one or more offered credential identifiers or credential configurations; - grant information for one or more supported issuance paths; - the authorisation parameters or pre-authorised grant information needed by the Wallet to continue the flow.
  2. The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a54a12a437505e5de785867e5dcc3d7a:<__None__> MAY support either: - Authorisation Code Flow; - Pre-Authorised Code Flow; or - both.

docs.title: 6.2.3 Credential Offer delivery and Wallet invocation
docs.text:
1. The Issuer delivers the offer to the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:cdd816f2320e175e35956b6cdcf8e70b:<__None__> by one of: - displaying a QR code; - providing a link; - invoking a same-device Wallet using a supported Wallet invocation mechanism.
  2. Issuers and Wallets SHALL support both same-device and cross-device delivery of 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:018a55e26fa12a2b373947065a794468:.
  3. For same-device, implementations SHALL support at least the custom URL scheme openid-credential-offer://.
  4. Implementations SHALL additionally support the custom URL scheme eu-eaa-offer://.
  5. For cross-device, implementations SHALL support delivery through a QR code carrying a valid 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:29e23ebe04bcaf2f8a2ff4167e18b3fd:<__None__> URI
  6. Additional wallet invocation mechanisms remain optional.

docs.title: 6.2.4 Wallet processes the offer
docs.text:
1. The Wallet receives the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:95ae7ede8bd73da9bf72f6ed3c0bab65:<__None__>.
  2. The Wallet parses the offer and determines: - the Issuer base URL; - offered credential configurations; - applicable grant information; - required authorisation parameters.
  3. The Wallet displays the offer to the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:767fb57ad98ad783a08fc4483aca77e9:<__None__> and asks for confirmation to proceed.

docs.title: 6.2.5 Authorisation Code Flow variant
docs.text:
1. Where the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a9f3cd4366b9f3c9a91683e236d7474e:<__None__> uses Authorisation Code Flow, the Wallet initiates the authorisation process using PAR.
  2. The Wallet follows the same Authorisation Code Flow defined in Section 6.1 for: - PAR; - user authorisation; - token acquisition; - credential request; - storage.
  3. The Wallet sends 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:f6db8624fdfafef2d920d8a866d4d34b: at the PAR and Token endpoints as described in Section 6.1.

docs.title: 6.2.6 Pre-Authorised Code Flow variant
docs.text:
1. Where the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:240c5949b605de626e526fe5fe7f71f2:<__None__> uses Pre-Authorised Code Flow, the Wallet does not perform a PAR request or browser-based authorisation redirect.
  2. The Wallet sends a token request to the Token Endpoint including: - grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code; - the pre-authorized_code; - a transaction code or user code where required by the offer or by the applicable profile; - WIA-based client authentication and DPoP sender-constraining material.
  3. The Token Endpoint validates the pre-authorised grant and returns: - a sender-constrained access_token; - optional refresh_token or other explicitly defined OAuth/OpenID4VCI parameters; - an optional DPoP-Nonce HTTP response header.
  4. The Wallet then proceeds to the Credential Endpoint as defined in Section 6.1.6.

docs.title: 6.2.7 Credential request
docs.text:
1. The Wallet sends a Credential Request or Batch Credential Request to the Credential Endpoint.
  2. The request includes: - Authorization: DPoP {access_token} and a DPoP proof bound to the access-token key; - the requested credential configuration information; - the applicable proof material; - Key Attestation (KA) where required by the selected proof method.
  3. The Issuer validates the request and either returns the credential or initiates deferred issuance.

docs.title: 6.2.8 Deferred issuance continuation
docs.text:
1. If issuance cannot be completed immediately, the Issuer returns the information required for deferred retrieval.
  2. The Wallet stores the transaction state and continues as defined in Section 6.3.

docs.title: 6.3 Deferred Credential Request
docs.text:
Deferred issuance allows the Issuer to complete credential production asynchronously while preserving the issuance transaction state.

  1. Where the Credential Endpoint cannot immediately return the credential, the Issuer returns the information needed for later retrieval, such as a transaction identifier and any endpoint or polling details required by the profile.
  2. The Wallet stores the deferred issuance state.
  3. The Wallet later calls the Deferred Credential Endpoint using the required access token and deferred issuance reference.
  4. The Issuer either: - returns the issued credential; - indicates that issuance is still pending; or - returns an error if the deferred issuance transaction cannot be completed.
  5. The Wallet repeats the retrieval only in accordance with the Issuer's indicated retry or polling guidance.
  6. Once the credential is returned, the Wallet validates and stores it as in Section 6.1.7.

docs.title: 7 Normative Requirements
docs.text:
This section defines the baseline normative requirements for APTITUDE implementations of the issuance profile.

Unless otherwise stated, the requirements in this section apply to issuance interactions only.

docs.title: 7.1 Common requirements (Wallet and Issuer)
docs.text:
Both Wallet and Issuer SHALL:

  1. Support OpenID4VCI 1.0 for credential issuance.
  2. Support metadata-based discovery.
  3. Support wallet-initiated issuance.
  4. Support issuer-initiated issuance via 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:87492f8706c46768c11fc4339e1b0fff:<__None__>.
  5. Support at least one of the following issuance grant types: - Authorisation Code Flow; - Pre-Authorised Code Flow.
  6. Support Authorisation Code Flow where the deployment requires 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:7d00d6cb2a79404661f9e2dd8d3cdcea:<__None__> authentication and interactive authorisation.
  7. Support Pre-Authorised Code Flow where the deployment profile or issuance scenario permits issuer-initiated issuance without an interactive authorisation redirect.
  8. Support DPoP as defined in RFC 9449 for sender-constraining access tokens and applicable HTTP requests.
  9. Support 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a80c6ef9e05b4bbf38dabb3694685ad9: / holder-binding during issuance, as required by the selected credential format and binding model.
  10. Support issuance-time metadata required to construct and process issuance requests.
  11. Support deferred issuance where the selected deployment profile or issuance process cannot always return the credential synchronously.
  12. Support the A128GCM and A256GCM algorithms in addition to the cryptographic suites required by OpenID4VC-HAIP.
  13. Support same-device Wallet invocation using the eu-eaa-offer:// custom URL scheme.

    14. Both Wallet and Issuer SHOULD:

    1. Support both immediate and deferred issuance responses.
    2. Support Batch Credential Requests where required by a more specific pilot or credential profile.
    3. If the Wallet supports issuance notifications and receives a notification_id from the Issuer, support one or more Notification Requests for that notification_id in accordance with the applicable notification mechanism.

    For issuance interactions using Authorisation Code Flow, both Wallet and Issuer SHALL additionally:

    1. Support Pushed Authorisation Requests (PAR).
    2. Support 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:bc874dda8cc491485aabaf86aeafcbd4:<__None__> with the S256 code challenge method.
    3. Support 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b41891c7e71dc1238bbc2d712364a950: handling at the PAR and Token endpoints.

docs.title: 7.2 Credential Offer
docs.text:
Issuers SHALL:

  1. Support 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c2c9aabf5505754fc0e8532238df8073: for issuer-initiated issuance.
  2. Include the credential_issuer identifier in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a342bdee94a2ea38753649a5251ae682:<__None__>.
  3. Include one or more offered credential identifiers or credential configuration identifiers sufficient for the Wallet to determine what is being offered.
  4. Include the grant information required by the Wallet to continue issuance.
  5. Support at least one of the following grant types in 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:bc41ada6f3254b5d9e2a5023653d4f99:: - authorization_code; - urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code.
  6. Include all grant-specific parameters needed by the Wallet to continue the flow.
  7. Ensure that the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b8c9e91762dcbd8494c1e97b0456cff5:<__None__> can be resolved consistently against Issuer metadata.
  8. For same-device invocation, support delivery using the eu-eaa-offer:// custom URL scheme.

    9. Issuers SHOULD:

    1. Support both same-device and cross-device offer delivery.
    2. Support QR-code-based delivery and URI-based invocation.
    3. Support 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:5c4fb4701a2c986a433f75e00eacd590: containing multiple offered credential configurations where the issuance scenario requires this.

      Wallets SHALL:

      1. Be able to parse 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:eadab13410a2280fa3b26f43812e8bc2: compliant with the applicable OpenID4VCI profile.
      2. Extract the Issuer identifier, offered credential configurations, and grant information.
      3. Determine from the offer whether the issuance path uses: - Authorisation Code Flow; - Pre-Authorised Code Flow; or - both.
      4. Use the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:f0ea8fdb4c81927726182a9fe15d9f81:<__None__> information consistently in later token and credential requests.
      5. Support same-device receipt via a supported Wallet invocation method.
      6. Support cross-device receipt via a QR code carrying a valid 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:07a80d5322ea42672659bdee847a1e66:<__None__> URI.
      7. Support same-device receipt via the eu-eaa-offer:// custom URL scheme.

        8. Wallets SHOULD:

        1. Validate that the offered credential identifiers or configurations are supported by the Issuer metadata before proceeding.
        2. Present the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c8d2df0f6852fd62268f33a309014c56:<__None__> to the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:ad024c87b6ab502a5a44a2e1ee9655dd:<__None__> in a way that makes the offered credentials and issuing party clear.

docs.title: 7.3 Authorisation Endpoint and PAR
docs.text:
This section applies only to issuance transactions using Authorisation Code Flow.

Issuers SHALL:

  1. Expose a PAR endpoint for issuance transactions using Authorisation Code Flow.
  2. Require PAR for all authorisation requests under this profile.
  3. Reject direct front-channel authorisation requests not preceded by PAR.
  4. Require the Wallet to include the credential-related authorisation parameters needed for the selected credential configuration and issuance path.
  5. Require 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:72f74704e7506d2653e9808775ebad70:<__None__> with S256.
  6. Require consistent use of client_id across PAR and Token requests.
  7. Require 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:44fa5ba89c04d958eb079064aef26452:<__None__> at the PAR endpoint.
  8. Require a DPoP proof signed by the private key corresponding to the public key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:429d88f3ad523059c1c5023fbb03e3d5: cnf claim.
  9. Verify that the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:3fe0481b6cb14aa5ff2b2e8de266e377: signature validates under the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:739b5f939f39e806991b23b3fc656bdf:<__None__> public key from the applicable trusted list.
  10. Verify that the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:7f44107bb5ac656e292df526da195a24: is not expired.
  11. Verify the DPoP proof under the public key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:fc668f1b91ceb21750be9b5ab3a7709c: cnf claim.

    Wallets SHALL:

    1. Use PAR for all Authorisation Code Flow requests under this profile.
    2. Include the required credential-related authorisation parameters.
    3. Include client_id, response_type=code, redirect_uri, state, and 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:0510963650750d3a16f62ee9ebecf69d:<__None__> parameters.
    4. Include 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:0447366b7b6f3a103d03684091791a5f: at the PAR endpoint.
    5. Include a DPoP proof signed by the key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:627cb24c12d66e49e09b1b74f34a3e53: cnf claim.
    6. Ensure that client_id is used consistently across PAR and Token requests.

      7. Wallets SHOULD:

      1. Check metadata in advance to determine whether additional authorisation parameters or authorization_details are required.
      2. Treat expired or rejected 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c6679d9865c62a6ad7450f0e2cf03d39: material as a recoverable client-authentication failure and obtain fresh attestation material before retrying.

docs.title: 7.4 Token Endpoint and Wallet Attestation
docs.text:
This section applies to both Authorisation Code Flow and Pre-Authorised Code Flow.

For Authorisation Code Flow, Wallets SHALL:

  1. Send a Token Request containing: - grant_type=authorization_code; - code; - redirect_uri; - code_verifier.
  2. Include 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:dc860a10f43ecc1e7d7477d9b6b2ff23: at the Token Endpoint.
  3. Include a DPoP proof signed by the key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:192b96911778dca728e56f78d152d534: cnf claim.
  4. Ensure consistency between the authenticated Wallet identity and the client_id used earlier in the transaction.

    5. For Pre-Authorised Code Flow, Wallets SHALL:

    1. Send a Token Request containing: - grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code; - the pre-authorized_code; - any transaction code or user code required by the offer or deployment profile.
    2. Include 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:aae8f19463bdaed6a063d1ae5694f1a0: and a DPoP proof signed by the key referenced in its cnf claim.
    3. Use the returned access token consistently in subsequent credential requests.

      4. Issuers SHALL:

      1. Expose a Token Endpoint.
      2. Validate the Token Request according to the applicable grant type.
      3. For Authorisation Code Flow, validate 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:8b0a2d9981e0e393218266ad3a317781:<__None__> inputs and authorisation-code state as required by OAuth/OpenID4VCI.
      4. Validate 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:5c613754d41a9172aaf7240a763eb8ad: and its associated DPoP proof: - the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:0bad30747f4c2bd4e4e2c88e5f8fe414: signature under the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:506ca2ca48697e2dce188d91e205f8f7:<__None__> public key from the applicable trusted list; - the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:1d50375b2f322d89e24d3b135b9db9fa: expiry; - the DPoP proof under the public key referenced in the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:ab1558dc9228dc8d982783b906a91ecf: cnf claim; - the DPoP htm, htu, iat, jti, and nonce claims as required by RFC 9449.
      5. Issue sender-constrained access tokens.
      6. Bind token usage to the Wallet according to the selected sender-constraining mechanism.
      7. Where a c_nonce is required for Credential Endpoint proof freshness, the Issuer SHALL expose the OpenID4VCI Nonce Endpoint. A c_nonce returned through another response, including a Token Response, SHALL NOT replace the Nonce Endpoint mechanism defined by this profile. The AS MAY return a DPoP-Nonce response header.

        8. Wallets SHALL obtain a fresh OpenID4VCI c_nonce from the Issuer's Nonce Endpoint immediately before generating Credential Endpoint proof material and SHALL NOT rely on a c_nonce received in a Token Response for that purpose.

        Issuers SHOULD:

        1. Support refresh tokens where long-lived issuance processes, renewal, or deferred issuance need them.
        2. Consider the sensitivity of the credential type before issuing long-lived refresh tokens.

        Wallets SHALL:

        1. Support sender-constrained token usage in subsequent calls to the Credential Endpoint.
        2. Handle an AS-provided DPoP-Nonce by placing it in the nonce claim of the subsequent DPoP proof. The Wallet obtains OpenID4VCI c_nonce from the Nonce Endpoint before generating credential proof material.

docs.title: 7.5 Credential Endpoint
docs.text:
Issuers SHALL:

  1. Expose a Credential Endpoint.
  2. Support issuance requests for the credential configurations published in Issuer metadata.
  3. Validate the access token and sender constraint.
  4. Validate the credential request syntax and requested credential configuration.
  5. For device-bound issuance, require the proofs parameter.
  6. Require that proofs contain either: - the jwt child member; or - the attestation child member.
  7. Validate the OpenID4VCI c_nonce and proof material according to the selected proof method.
  8. Validate Key Attestation (KA) according to the selected proof method before issuing a device-bound credential.
  9. Where applicable regulatory or trust rules provide KA status information, validate that status before issuing a device-bound credential and ensure that the issued credential does not outlive the relevant WIA or KA status-maintenance commitments.
  10. Return either the issued credential or a deferred issuance response.

Wallets SHALL:

  1. Send a Credential Request containing the requested credential configuration or other format-specific request parameters.
  2. For device-bound issuance, include the proofs parameter.
  3. Populate proofs using either: - proofs.jwt; or - proofs.attestation; according to the selected binding model and issuer requirements.
  4. Obtain and use a fresh OpenID4VCI c_nonce from the Issuer's 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:dabc086920cebb31e8dd225297595a23:<__None__> Endpoint immediately before generating credential proof material.
  5. Include a DPoP proof in the Credential Endpoint request, using the access-token-bound key and any Resource Server-provided DPoP-Nonce.
  6. Validate the returned credential, including issuer binding and format-specific integrity checks.
  7. Store only credentials that have successfully passed Wallet validation.

docs.title: 7.5.1 Credential Request using proofs.jwt
docs.text:
Wallets SHALL:

  1. Include exactly one element in the jwt array.
  2. Include a valid OpenID4VCI c_nonce claim in the proof JWT body, obtained from the Issuer's 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:1e54e15562b0f3332054eaa1e59448a2:<__None__> Endpoint.
  3. Include the key_attestation protected header parameter.
  4. Carry the Key Attestation (KA) in that key_attestation parameter and include the same issuer-provided c_nonce in the KA's nonce claim.
  5. Ensure that the KA contains one or more attested public keys owned by the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b06da279c9b5f5a5c707981348a29c1a:<__None__>.
  6. Sign the JWT using the private key corresponding to the first public key in the attested_keys claim of the KA.

Issuers SHALL:

  1. Verify that the KA signature in key_attestation validates under the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:e314a3abfa4fa333abf61ec745c62fe9:<__None__> public key from the applicable trusted list.
  2. Verify that the JWT signature validates under the first public key in the attested_keys array of the KA.
  3. Verify that the proof JWT contains a valid OpenID4VCI c_nonce from the Issuer's 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:3a1dab1deb6f7ab5a68b2d4be4740dd4:<__None__> Endpoint and that the KA carries the same value in its nonce claim.
  4. Generate as many credentials as there are attested public keys in the KA, where the applicable profile requires multi-key issuance.
  5. Bind each issued credential to one of the attested public keys.
  6. Ensure that no two issued credentials in the transaction are bound to the same public key.

docs.title: 7.5.2 Credential Request using proofs.attestation
docs.text:
Wallets SHALL:

  1. Include exactly one element in the attestation array.
  2. Include the OpenID4VCI c_nonce obtained from the Issuer's 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:2846652d7246114ebecd5695243a7069:<__None__> Endpoint in the KA's nonce claim.
  3. Carry the Key Attestation (KA) directly as the single attestation element.

Issuers SHALL:

  1. Verify that the KA signature validates under the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b085fb11824ad89307ac196e1e418be8:<__None__> public key from the applicable trusted list and that its nonce claim contains the current OpenID4VCI c_nonce.
  2. Generate as many credentials as there are attested public keys in the KA, where the applicable profile requires multi-key issuance.
  3. Bind each issued credential to one of the attested public keys.
  4. Ensure that no two issued credentials in the transaction are bound to the same public key.

Issuers SHOULD:

  1. Reject malformed or semantically inconsistent proofs structures with explicit error information where possible.
  2. Distinguish clearly between c_nonce failure, DPoP-Nonce failure, attestation failure, proof failure, and policy failure.

docs.title: 7.6 Deferred Credential Endpoint
docs.text:
Issuers SHALL:

  1. Expose a Deferred Credential Endpoint where the deployment supports deferred issuance.
  2. Return the information needed by the Wallet to retrieve deferred credentials.
  3. Validate deferred retrieval tokens, references, or transaction identifiers.
  4. Publish the Deferred Credential Endpoint in metadata where supported.
  5. Return explicit terminal errors for expired, denied, or otherwise failed deferred issuance transactions.

Issuers SHOULD:

  1. Provide retry guidance or polling hints.
  2. Preserve transaction state for a duration appropriate to the issuance process.

Wallets SHALL:

  1. Recognise deferred issuance responses.
  2. Persist the transaction state needed to continue deferred retrieval.
  3. Poll or retry according to the Issuer's guidance until completion or terminal failure.
  4. Distinguish pending and failed issuance states in Wallet behaviour.
  5. Use Authorization: DPoP {access_token} and a DPoP proof bound to the access-token key for deferred retrieval.

Wallets SHOULD:

  1. Apply retry intervals and back-off.
  2. Allow the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:ebe4ec9a1a83e0091bd1ca960ad13d5d:<__None__> to stop retrying or resume later.

docs.title: 7.7 Server Metadata
docs.text:
Issuers SHALL publish metadata that includes:

  1. OAuth 2.0 / OpenID configuration, including Authorisation, Token, and PAR endpoints.
  2. 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:58cf3ebd3cce01414f69a4d1c057383f: metadata describing supported credential configurations.
  3. The Credential Endpoint location.
  4. The Deferred Credential Endpoint location, where supported.
  5. Any relevant proof types, credential format support, and associated configuration data required by Wallets.
  6. The format identifiers for SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc.
  7. Signed Issuer Metadata whose JWS protected header carries the Issuer access certificate in x5c.
  8. The issuer_info metadata parameter carrying issuer registration material, including the registration certificate and registrar dataset, as profiled by ETSI.

    9. Wallets SHALL:

    1. Retrieve and process Issuer metadata.
    2. Use metadata to construct authorisation and credential requests.
    3. Use metadata to interpret 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:4d751a62c1f809801facb9866b7fac54: and supported credential configurations.
    4. Where notification support is implemented and the Issuer provides a notification_id, use Issuer metadata or the applicable profile to determine how Notification Requests are sent.
    5. Process signed Issuer Metadata x5c and issuer_info content as part of issuer validation and registration-material handling.

docs.title: 8 Interface Definitions
docs.text: This section defines the logical interfaces for conformance testing. Exact URL paths are deployment-specific and discovered through metadata.

docs.title: 8.1 Wallet Invocation Interface
docs.text:
• Direction: Issuer to Wallet
  • Transport: custom URI, QR code, or equivalent Wallet invocation mechanism

Wallets and Issuers SHOULD support at least one interoperable Wallet invocation method suitable for both same-device and cross-device use.

The same-device invocation method SHALL include the eu-eaa-offer:// custom URL scheme.

docs.title: 8.2 Credential Offer Interface
docs.text:
• Direction: Issuer to Wallet

The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:b32781ef7a6902a2d7a7b79315017149:<__None__> SHALL contain at least:

  • credential_issuer;
  • grant information;
  • credential identifiers or credential configuration identifiers;
  • the information the Wallet needs to continue the issuance flow.

The exact JSON structure SHALL comply with OpenID4VCI.

docs.title: 8.3 PAR Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Issuer (AS)
  • Method: POST

docs.title: Request (logical fields)
docs.text:
• client_id
  • credential-related authorisation parameters
  • code_challenge
  • code_challenge_method=S256
  • redirect_uri
  • response_type=code
  • state
  • WIA client authentication and DPoP proof

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• request_uri
  • expires_in
  • optional DPoP-Nonce HTTP response header

docs.title: 8.4 Token Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Issuer (AS)
  • Method: POST

docs.title: Request (logical fields)
docs.text:
• grant_type=authorization_code or grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code
  • code, redirect_uri, and code_verifier for Authorization Code Flow
  • pre-authorized_code and any required transaction code for Pre-Authorized Code Flow
  • OAuth-Client-Attestation: <WIA>
  • DPoP: <proof>

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• access_token
  • token_type=DPoP
  • expires_in
  • optional refresh_token or other explicitly defined OAuth/OpenID4VCI parameters
  • optional DPoP-Nonce HTTP response header

docs.title: 8.5 Credential Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Issuer
  • Method: POST

docs.title: Request (logical fields)
docs.text:
• Authorization: DPoP {access_token}
  • requested credential configuration or identifier
  • format-specific request information
  • proof material, including KA where device binding is used
  • DPoP: <proof>

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• issued credential(s), or
  • deferred issuance response

docs.title: 8.6 Nonce Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Issuer
  • Method: POST or as defined by metadata/profile

The Nonce Endpoint returns OpenID4VCI c_nonce in its JSON response. The Wallet obtains c_nonce immediately before generating Credential Endpoint proof material or KA. A Resource Server MAY independently return a DPoP-Nonce HTTP response header for DPoP proof freshness; DPoP-Nonce and c_nonce are separate values and mechanisms.

docs.title: 8.7 Notification Interface
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Issuer
  • Method: POST or as defined by metadata/profile

If the deployment supports issuance notifications and the Issuer provides a notification_id, the Wallet SHOULD send one or more Notification Requests for that notification_id using the mechanism defined by the applicable profile or Issuer metadata.

docs.title: 8.8 Deferred Credential Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Issuer
  • Method: POST

docs.title: Request (logical fields)
docs.text:
• Authorization: DPoP {access_token}
  • DPoP: <proof> bound to the access-token key
  • transaction identifier, where applicable

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• issued credential(s), or
  • pending status with retry guidance, or
  • terminal failure

docs.title: 8.9 Metadata Endpoints
docs.text:
Issuers SHALL publish:

  • OAuth / OpenID discovery metadata;
  • 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:557704d16845a7a8dea7550a5c0e8498: metadata.

    Metadata SHALL provide enough information for a conforming Wallet to discover and use:

    • authorisation endpoint;
    • token endpoint;
    • PAR endpoint;
    • credential endpoint;
    • deferred credential endpoint, where applicable;
    • supported credential configurations;
    • supported proof types and formats;
    • the Authorization Server issuer identifier, using authorization_servers when present or the Credential Issuer identifier otherwise;
    • dpop_signing_alg_values_supported and other applicable Authorization Server capabilities.
    • token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported containing attest_jwt_client_auth_dpop;
    • client_attestation_pop_methods_supported containing dpop_combined.

    The metadata set SHALL additionally provide signed Issuer Metadata with the Issuer access certificate transported in the JWS protected header x5c, and the issuer_info metadata parameter carrying issuer registration material, including the registration certificate and registrar dataset, as profiled by ETSI.

docs.title: 9 Conformance
docs.text:
An implementation conforms to this specification as a Wallet if it:

  1. Implements the Wallet requirements in Sections 6 and 7
  2. Supports the Wallet-side interfaces and behaviours defined in Section 8
  3. Uses OpenID4VCI 1.0 and the APTITUDE issuance profile constraints defined in this RFC.

An implementation conforms to this specification as an Issuer if it:

  1. Implements the Issuer requirements in Sections 6 and 7
  2. Publishes the required metadata.
  3. Provides the issuance interfaces defined in Section 8
  4. Applies the APTITUDE issuance baseline consistently across supported credential configurations.

Pilot-specific profiles MAY define additional constraints for specific credential types or domains. Such profiles SHALL NOT relax the mandatory requirements in this document.

9.1 Scope of the Conformance Matrix

This conformance matrix verifies baseline protocol interoperability between an Issuer or 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:a7ac87290d4ccb8601b1c516ef2f789b:<__None__> under test and the reference issuance endpoints defined by this APTITUDE Issuance Profile. It is intended to confirm correct support for representative OpenID4VCI v1.0 issuance flows covered by this RFC, including wallet-initiated and issuer-initiated issuance.

The matrix is a protocol interoperability matrix, not a complete ARF v3.0.0 or CIR 2024/2982 / CIR 2024/2979 / CIR 2024/2977 compliance assessment. It focuses on issuance flow processing, 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:c594f4ac70d0f83f49c27b15b25ad4a0:<__None__> handling, PAR-based authorisation, token acquisition, proof-bound credential requests, deferred issuance handling, and metadata-driven endpoint use within the scope of this profile.

It does not exhaustively test broader trust, governance, semantic, privacy, supervisory, or deployment-specific obligations. Where ARF v3.0.0 or CIR identifiers are included, they provide traceability and alignment for the issuance interoperability capability being exercised, rather than full normative coverage of the broader requirement domain. This is consistent with the RFC’s explicitly horizontal, cross-pilot scope and its stated out-of-scope exclusions.
