docs.title: APTITUDE RFC-03 Trust Evaluation
docs.text: Status: v0.1 Type: Cross-pilot baseline RFC Scope: Trust establishment and trust evaluation Related profiles: APTITUDE Trust Specifications Companion RFC: RFC-04 Revocation

docs.title: Authors
docs.text: Andrea Moro (Fondazione Bruno Kessler - Center for Cybersecurity)

docs.title: Reviewers
docs.text: Nikos Triantafyllou, University of Aegean; Leif Johansson, SIROS Fundation.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
This document defines the APTITUDE Trust Evaluation Profile for interoperable trust evaluation across the APTITUDE pilots.

It profiles the trust evaluation processes defined by the APTITUDE Trust Specifications. The profile separates common trust operations from checks that are specific to WRPAC authentication, WRPRC authorization, Register responses, and signatures or seals on attestations.

The detailed source processes are the Authentication Process, X.509 Certificate Chain Validation, and Sign/Seal Validation Process in the Trust Evaluation Process section. These are:

  • Trust Anchor Validation;
  • Authentication Validation;
  • Authorization Validation
  • Signature Validation

The purpose of this RFC is to define:

  • the common validation of Trust Artifacts:

  • the WRPAC validation used to authenticate a WRP;

  • the mandatory WRPRC and optional Register-response checks used to establish authorization context;

  • the Sign/Seal Certificate and attestation signature validation checks;

  • interfaces and conformance checks that can be converted into ITB+ test cases.

This RFC is a cross-pilot baseline. A pilot MAY add stricter requirements, but it SHALL NOT weaken the mandatory checks defined here.

docs.title: 2. Scope
docs.text:
This RFC covers the following trust evaluation layers:

  1. Trust-source validation: validation of the applicable List of Trusted Entities (LoTE), followed by extraction of a Trust Anchor from ServiceDigitalIdentity.
  2. Common X.509 validation: validation of a certificate path against the extracted Trust Anchor.
  3. WRPAC validation: authentication of a WRP using its WRPAC and a signature over the interaction artifact.
  4. WRPRC validation: validation of the WRP registration certificate as authorization evidence.
  5. Register-response validation: optional validation of the applicable signed or sealed Registrar response in addition to the WRPRC.
  6. Sign/Seal validation: validation of the certificate used to sign or seal an Attestation and verification of the Attestation signature or seal.

APTITUDE profiles use LoTEs only. They do not use a List of Trusted Lists (LOTL), a national Trusted List (TL), or a LOTL-to-TL discovery hierarchy. A LoTE MAY be published in JSON or XML, as specified for its entity type.

Each entity type SHALL have a dedicated LoTE. WP2 SHALL manage and publish the LoTEs used by that pilot, including the relevant publication endpoints and applicable profiles. The applicable LoTE is selected by the artifact or entity type being validated.

The QTSPs Trust Anchors SHALL be published in a dedicated QEAA-provider LoTE. The pilot is expected to publish this LoTE in XML; the final XML publication and signature profile remain a WP2 configuration point.

This RFC includes baseline requirements for:

  • Wallet Units;
  • Wallet Relying Parties;
  • Providers of WRPAC and WRPRC;
  • Attestation and PID Providers;
  • LoTE management and publication by the WP2 lead organization;
  • Registrars and Registers.

This RFC does not define:

  • sector-specific certificate semantics, which are defined by the relevant WRPAC, WRPRC, and Sign/Seal Certificate profiles;
  • the administrative lifecycle of entities and Trust Anchors;
  • revocation mechanisms or revocation endpoint protocols, which are outside this document's detailed scope and SHALL be referenced through RFC004;
  • pilot-specific user-interface requirements;
  • detailed implementation assertions beyond the conformance catalogue in this document.

docs.title: 3. Normative Language
docs.text: The key words SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, MAY, and OPTIONAL in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.

docs.title: 4.1 Wallet Unit
docs.text: The Wallet Unit, including its, performs the trust evaluation on behalf of the User.

docs.title: 4.2 Wallet Relying Party
docs.text: The Wallet Relying Party (WRP) is the entity authenticated with a WRPAC. Depending on the interaction, it may be a direct Relying Party or a Relying Party Intermediary.

docs.title: 4.3 Provider of WRPAC
docs.text: The Provider of WRPAC issues WRPACs. Its Trust Anchor certificates SHALL be published in the dedicated WRPAC-provider LoTE.

docs.title: 4.4 Provider of WRPRC
docs.text: The Provider of WRPRC issues WRPRCs. Its Trust Anchor certificates SHALL be published in the dedicated WRPRC-provider LoTE.

docs.title: 4.5 Attestation Provider and QTSP
docs.text: An Attestation Provider issues an Attestation and signs or seals it using a Sign/Seal Certificate. The Trust Anchor certificates for the applicable Sign/Seal Certificate issuers SHALL be published in the LoTE dedicated to the relevant entity type, including the QEAA-provider LoTE for QEAA providers.

docs.title: 4.6 LoTE Publisher
docs.text: The LoTE Publisher is the WP2 trust group within the pilot. It SHALL manage and publish one LoTE per configured entity type and SHALL make the applicable format and endpoint available to relying implementations.

docs.title: 4.7 Registrar
docs.text: The Registrar and its APIs are managed and published the WP2 trust group within the pilot. This service stores WRP registration data and exposes the Register API. The Registrar's Trust Anchor certificates SHALL be published in the dedicated Registrar and Register LoTE.

docs.title: 5.1 Entity-Type LoTE Model
docs.text:
The following table defines the minimum LoTE separation for this profile.

Entity type Trust source Expected format Used to validate Wallet Providers Wallet Provider LoTE JSON WUAs, WIAs, and related wallet artifacts PID Providers PID Provider LoTE JSON PID signatures PuB-EAA Providers PuB-EAA Provider LoTE JSON PuB-EAA signatures Providers of WRPAC WRPAC-provider LoTE JSON WRPAC chains Providers of WRPRC WRPRC-provider LoTE JSON WRPRC signatures and chains Registrars and Registers Registrar and Register LoTE JSON Register responses QEAA providers and QTSPs QEAA-provider LoTE XML QEAA Sign/Seal Certificates EAA Providers EAA Provider LoTE JSON EAA signatures

All LoTEs use the TS 119 602 data model. TS 119 615 is used as the procedural basis for validating the LoTE structure, integrity, freshness, and trust chain. The JSON and XML signature or seal mechanisms differ; this RFC requires the applicable format-specific signature or seal verification but does not duplicate its detailed mechanics.

docs.title: 5.2 Validation Flow
docs.text:
The common sequence for WRP trust evaluation is:

  1. Apply the artifact-specific signature and content checks.
  2. Select the LoTE for the entity type.
  3. Retrieve and validate the LoTE.
  4. Extract the entity's Trust Anchor from ServiceDigitalIdentity.
  5. Apply the common X.509 path validation to the presented certificate chain.
  6. Apply the revocation checks defined by RFC004, wherever required.

Steps 5. and 6. SHALL be executed whenever validation of the specific Trust Artifact requires validation of an X.509 trust chain or a status check.

Successful completion of an intermediate step permits only continuation to the remaining applicable checks. A Wallet Unit or WRP SHALL NOT output a final AUTHENTICATED, AUTHORIZED, or ACCEPTED result until all applicable trust, path-validation, and status checks have succeeded.

  • To Authenticate a WRP,

  • Step 1. is applied to the Credential Issuer Metadata, or Presentation Request, depending on the flow using the public key within the WRPAC transmitted within the artifact.

  • Steps 2., 3., 4. are applied to the WRPAC Provider LoTE.

  • Steps 5., 6. are applied to the WRPAC and its X.509 chain.

  • To Authorize a WRP,

  • Step 1. is applied to the mandatory WRPRC transmitted in the Credential Issuer Metadata or Presentation Request. When optional Register-response validation is invoked, the applicable syntax, signature, pertinence, and consistency checks are also applied to the Register response. Step 1. is divided into (i) syntax and signature validation, (ii) authorization checks comprising WRPAC binding, issuance or presentation binding, entitlement verification, and EDP validation, and (iii) the applicable user-override behavior. These checks are described in the Authorization Process Profile.

  • Steps 2., 3., 4. are applied to the WRPRC Provider LoTE and, when optional Register-response validation is invoked, to the Registrar LoTE.
  • Step 5. is applied to the WRPRC signing certificate and its X.509 chain and, when optional Register-response validation is invoked, to the Register-response signing certificate and its X.509 chain.

  • Step 6. is applied to both the WRPRC and (if needed) the WRPRC signing certificate and its X.509 chain. When optional Register-response validation is invoked, Step 6. is also applied to the Register-response signing certificate and its X.509 chain wherever required by RFC004.

  • To Validate the Signature of a WIA, KA, PID, QEAA, EAA, PuB-EAA,

  • Step 1. is applied to the Attestation using the public key within the Sign/Seal Certificate transmitted within the Attestation itself.

  • Steps 2., 3., 4. are applied to the specific Entity LoTE.
  • Steps 5., 6. are applied to the Sign/Seal Certificate and its X.509 chain.
  • Step 6. is applied to both the Attestation and the Sign/Seal certificate and its X.509 chain.

docs.title: 6. Normative Requirements
docs.text: Unless otherwise stated, these requirements apply to trust evaluation interactions.

docs.title: 6.1 Wallet Unit Requirements
docs.text:
A Wallet Unit or WRP conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • support validation of JSON and XML LoTEs according to the applicable entity-type profile as specified in Trust Anchor Validation;
  • select the LoTE according to the type of entity or Attestation being validated;
  • retrieve the Trust Anchor from the validated LoTE ServiceDigitalIdentity;
  • implement the common X.509 path validation in the X.509 Certificate Chain Validation process in the Trust Evaluation Process;
  • perform WRPAC validation as specified in Authentication Validation;
  • validate a WRPRC as specified in Authorization Validation;
  • perform Sign/Seal Certificate and Attestation signature validation as specified in the Trust Evaluation Process;

A Wallet Unit or WRP MAY support optional Register-response validation. When it invokes this validation, it SHALL validate the response as specified in Register Response Validation.

For this profile, references to Authorization Validation do not make Register-response validation or Register fallback mandatory. A missing or invalid mandatory WRPRC SHALL fail authorization.

docs.title: 6.2 WP2 Operated Entities
docs.text:
A Provider of WRPAC, WRPRC, or Sign/Seal Certificates SHALL:

  • be represented in the dedicated entity-type LoTE;
  • publish the Trust Anchor certificate in its ServiceDigitalIdentity;
  • ensure that certificate identity data is consistent with the entity identity in the LoTE;
  • expose the endpoint or service required by the applicable artifact profile, including revocation checks.

The LoTE Publisher SHALL:

  • manage and publish one LoTE per entity type used by the pilot;
  • publish each LoTE in its declared JSON or XML format;
  • maintain the integrity, authenticity, and freshness information required by the applicable LoTE profile;
  • publish the QEAA-provider/QTSP Trust Anchors in the dedicated QEAA-provider LoTE;
  • make the LoTE endpoint and format discoverable to relying implementations.

A Registrar SHALL:

  • be represented in the dedicated Registrar and Register LoTE;
  • publish or expose the Register API according to the Register API OAS;
  • return signed or sealed responses that can be verified with a Trust Anchor in the Registrar and Register LoTE.

docs.title: 7. Interface Definitions
docs.text: These interfaces define the minimum observable behavior for conformance testing.

docs.title: 7.1 LoTE Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet Unit or WRP to the LoTE Publisher.
  • Method: GET

The Wallet unit SHALL retrieve the LoTE for the entity type being validated.

The endpoint URI and media type SHALL be the ones published by the WP2 lead organization for that entity type. A request SHALL include:

  • Host, containing the endpoint hostname;
  • Accept: application/json for a JSON LoTE, or Accept: application/xml for an XML LoTE.

A successful response SHALL:

  • return 200 OK;
  • set Content-Type to the corresponding JSON or XML media type;
  • contain a structurally valid TS 119 602 LoTE;
  • contain the signature or seal required by the published format profile.

The Wallet Unit SHALL perform the LoTE validation required by Section 6.1 and Trust Anchor Validation before using any Trust Anchor from the response.

docs.title: 7.2 Register Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet Unit to Registrar/Register API.
  • Method: GET
  • Authentication: Public query access, unless the applicable API profile requires otherwise.

The endpoint SHALL be implemented according to the Register API OAS.

Use of this endpoint is OPTIONAL for Wallet Unit and WRP conformance. When a Wallet Unit invokes optional Register-response validation, it SHALL construct a query containing the WRP identifier and the context-specific intended-use or Attestation information. The response SHALL:

  • return the status defined by the API for the query result;
  • return a signed or sealed response for a successful query;
  • use the media type specified by the OAS;
  • be validated according to Section 6.1 and Register Response Validation.

An HTTP success status alone SHALL NOT make a Register response trusted.

If the response is unavailable or fails authenticity, integrity, or pertinence validation, the Wallet Unit SHALL discard it and continue authorization using the valid mandatory WRPRC. If a response passes those checks but is inconsistent with the mandatory WRPRC, the Wallet Unit SHALL fail authorization and SHALL NOT offer a user override.

docs.title: 8. Security Considerations
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL use HTTPS for LoTE and Register retrieval and MAY apply caching and endpoint privacy measures consistent with the applicable pilot profile.

Trust Anchors SHALL NOT be accepted from an unvalidated LoTE or from self-declared interaction data.

Certificates and Certificate chains SHALL NOT be accepted solely because a leaf signature verifies.

docs.title: 9. Conformance
docs.text:
A Wallet Solution or WRP implementation conforms to this RFC if:

  1. implements the requirements in Section 6.1;
  2. implements the LoTE interface in Section 7.1 and, if it claims optional Register-response validation, the Register interface in Section 7.2;
  3. passes the common, WRPAC, mandatory WRPRC, and Sign/Seal checks in Section 10, and passes the optional Register-response checks if it claims that capability.

docs.title: 10. Conformance Check Catalogue and Test Matrix

docs.title: APTITUDE RFC-04 Revocation
docs.text: Status: v0.1 Type: Cross-pilot baseline RFC Scope: Artifact Status Establishment Target protocols: OCSP, CRL, Status List Token Related profiles: APTITUDE Trust Specifications Companion RFC: RFC-03 Trust Establishment

docs.title: Authors
docs.text: Andrea Moro (Fondazione Bruno Kessler)

docs.title: Reviewers
docs.text: Nikos Triantafyllou, University of Aegean; Giancarlo Degani, Infocert; Aleksandar Simsic, ICTU.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
This document defines the APTITUDE Trust Artifact Status Profile for interoperable status establishment and revocation checking across APTITUDE pilots.

It specifies a baseline, cross-pilot profile for the validation of trust artifacts aligned with the APTITUDE Trust Specifications, the references therein, and the ARF.

The purpose of this RFC is to establish a stable starting point for interoperability across APTITUDE pilots by defining:

  • impacted roles and components;
  • normative requirements for X.509 chain revocation checking of WRPAC and Sign/Seal certificates and Status List Token validation of WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials (PID/QEAA, EAA, and PuB-EAA);
  • interface definitions for the relevant protocols (OCSP, CRL, Status List Token);
  • a conformance check catalogue that maps the normative requirements into verifiable checks;
  • a test case matrix that maps the conformance checks into executable test cases for the ITB+ conformance test cases.

This RFC is intended to support interoperability first. Pilot-specific or sector-specific extensions may be added later, but they should not weaken the baseline requirements defined here.

docs.title: 2. Scope
docs.text:
This RFC profiles status establishment and revocation checking under three normative tracks:

  • OCSP track -- X.509 chain revocation checking using RFC 6960. OCSP is mandatory for Sign/Seal certificate chains and optional for WRPAC chains;
  • CRL track -- X.509 chain revocation checking for WRPAC chains, profiled under ETSI TS 119 411-8 and RFC 5280. CRL support is mandatory for WRPACs;
  • TSL track -- status establishment and revocation checking for WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials (PID, QEAA, EAA, and PuB-EAA), profiled under the applicable APTITUDE Rulebooks, ETSI profiles and the IETF Token Status List draft-21.

In this RFC, X.509 chain revocation checking means determining the revocation status of every certificate in the relevant X.509 certification path, including the WRPAC or Sign/Seal certificate and any revocable issuing or intermediate certificates. This checking is used to validate whether the WRPAC or Sign/Seal certificate can be trusted for the intended operation. It is performed with mandatory CRL and optional OCSP for WRPAC chains, and mandatory OCSP for Sign/Seal certificate chains.

This RFC includes baseline requirements for:

  • generation of OCSP Requests;
  • generation of OCSP Response and their verification;
  • CRL parsing and verification;
  • Status List Token parsing and verification for WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials.

This RFC does not define:

  • sector-specific certificate semantics (already defined in WRPAC profile and WRPRC profile);
  • the lifecycle of the entities and related Trust Artifacts (already defined in Trust Management);
  • revocation artifacts and semantics (already defined in Revocation Menchanisms);
  • pilot-specific UI requirements;
  • detailed test assertions; (these are derived into the ITB+ test suite from the requirements matrix in this document).

docs.title: 3. Normative Language
docs.text: The key words SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, MAY, and OPTIONAL in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.

docs.title: 4.1 Wallet-Relying Party
docs.text: The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:d8929e463c751001b40209ae6c167537:, as defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with the ARF notions of Relying Party, Attestation Provider and PID Provider. In this RFC, it is the entity to whom the WRPAC and WRPRC refers.

docs.title: 4.2 Wallet Unit
docs.text: The Wallet Unit is the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:3cec37c27de7cf8492ffb596284e5921:<__None__> as defined in the ARF and APTITUDE glossary, including one or more 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:29e5c628510969348c54614e121544e2: on the Holder’s device or environment. In this RFC, the term Wallet refers to the Wallet Unit (and its Wallet Instances) when the distinction is not material, acting on behalf of the 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:5b3fa14de114b8f2ddcac13833b9b635: to perform X.509 chain revocation checking for WRPAC and Sign/Seal certificates, and Status List Token validation for WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials.

docs.title: 4.3 Provider of WRPAC
docs.text: The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:f74f16ca7f0aedb8eb67614862fa273a:, as defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with the ARF notion of Provider of WRPAC, is the entity issuing WRPAC and the related status services: a mandatory CRL endpoint and, optionally, an OCSP responder.

docs.title: 4.4 Provider of WRPRC
docs.text: The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:89a22cba0a1ea00e9dc8b7e587c44c13:, as defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with the ARF notion of Provider of WRPRC, is the entity issuing WRPRC and the related status Services (Status List Token endpoint).

docs.title: 4.5 Wallet Provider
docs.text: The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:28032ca5cb9248e74a562130b96ff62f: (WP), as defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with the ARF notion of Wallet Provider, is the entity providing Wallet Solutions. For the purposes of this RFC, the WP is responsible for issuing and cryptographically signing Wallet Unit Attestations, including WIAs and KAs, and for managing their lifecycle and revocation through Status List Tokens.

docs.title: 4.6 Attestation Provider
docs.text: The 6251a85a-47d0-11ee-be56-0242ac120002:376eb2c326dd0f69523700e13c649c7c: (AP), as defined in the APTITUDE glossary and aligned with the ARF notion of Attestation Provider, is the entity issuing Digital Credentials. For the purposes of this RFC, the applicable AP is responsible for issuing and cryptographically signing PID, QEAA, EAA, and PuB-EAA attestations and for managing their lifecycle and revocation through Status List Tokens.

docs.title: 4.7 Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates
docs.text:
The Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates is the Certificate Authority or Qualified Trust Service Provider responsible for issuing and managing the Sign/Seal Certificates used by Wallet Providers, PID Providers, and Attestation Providers. Sign/Seal Certificates and their certificate paths are profiled in the applicable EUDI Wallet certificate-profile specifications, including ETSI TS 119 412-6.

In this RFC, the Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates is responsible for ensuring that the revocation status of every revocable certificate in a Sign/Seal certificate path can be checked using the mandatory OCSP track. The Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates may also provide CRLs as a supplementary mechanism, but CRL availability does not replace the mandatory OCSP requirement.

docs.title: 5. High-Level Flows
docs.text: The high-level flows for X.509 chain revocation checking of WRPAC and Sign/Seal certificates, and for Status List Token validation of WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials, can be found in Revocation Checking.

docs.title: 6. Normative Requirements
docs.text:
This section defines the baseline normative requirements for APTITUDE implementations of the status-establishment and revocation-checking profile.

Unless otherwise stated, the requirements in this section apply whenever a Wallet establishes or checks the status of a WRPAC, WRPRC, WIA, KA, Digital Credential, or Sign/Seal certificate. The primary use case is an Entity (either a Wallet Instance or Wallet-Relying Party) validating trust artifacts or attestations during issuance or presentation flows.

docs.title: 6.1 Wallet Solution Requirements
docs.text:
A Wallet Solution conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • Support RFC 5280 for CRL parsing and validation of WRPAC certificate chains;
  • Support RFC 6960 for OCSP request generation and response parsing and validation of Sign/Seal certificate chains;
  • Support the IETF Token Status List draft-21 for Status List Token parsing and validation for WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials;
  • support JWT and CWT representations of Status List Tokens as required by the applicable TSL profile;

A Wallet Solution conforming to this RFC MAY:

  • Support RFC 6960 for optional OCSP request generation and response parsing and validation of WRPAC certificate chains, as defined in OCSP request.

docs.title: 6.2 Provider of WRPAC Requirements
docs.text:
A WRPAC Provider conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • expose at least a CRL endpoint as described in section CRL Endpoint;
  • generate the CRL listing all revoked WRPAC certificates covered by the WRPAC certificate chain with the semantics defined in CRL.

A WRPAC Provider conforming to this RFC MAY:

  • expose the OCSP endpoint as described in section OCSP Endpoint with OCSP responses conforming to OCSP response.

Note: OCSP support is optional for conformance. A WRPAC Provider that does not expose an OCSP endpoint conforms through the mandatory CRL track.

docs.title: 6.3 Provider of WRPRC Requirements
docs.text:
A WRPRC Provider conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • expose a Status List Token endpoint as described in section SLT Endpoint;
  • act as both the Status Issuer and the Status Provider for its WRPRCs;
  • generate and maintain the Status List, listing the status of all issued WRPRCs, and embed it into a Status List Token as defined in the IETF Token Status List draft-21;
  • ensure that revocation of a WRPRC is reflected in the Status List without undue delay.

docs.title: 6.4 Wallet Provider Requirements
docs.text:
A Wallet Provider conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • issue and cryptographically sign the WIAs and KAs that it provides;
  • allocate each issued WIA and KA a distinct, non-negative idx value and include the corresponding Status List reference in the location defined by the Wallet Unit Attestation Profile;
  • implement the Wallet Unit Attestation TSL profile in Section 10.1.1, including its status encoding, SLT generation, signing, compression, and publication requirements;
  • act as both the Status Issuer and the Status Provider for its WIAs and KAs;
  • expose a Status List Token endpoint as described in section SLT Endpoint;
  • generate and maintain Status Lists containing the status of its issued WIAs and KAs, and embed them into Status List Tokens as defined in the IETF Token Status List draft-21;
  • manage the lifecycle and revocation of its WIAs and KAs and reflect each status change in the applicable Status List without undue delay.

docs.title: 6.5 Attestation Provider Requirements
docs.text:
An Attestation Provider conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • issue and cryptographically sign the issued PID, QEAA, EAA, and PuB-EAA depending on the type of Digital Credentials it provides;
  • allocate each issued Digital Credential a distinct, non-negative idx value and include the corresponding Status List reference in the location defined by the Digital Credentials Profile;
  • implement the Digital Credentials TSL profile in Section 10.1.2, including its status encoding, SLT generation, signing, compression, and publication requirements;
  • act as both the Status Issuer and the Status Provider for its Digital Credentials;
  • expose a Status List Token endpoint as described in section SLT Endpoint;
  • generate and maintain Status Lists containing the status of its issued Digital Credentials, and embed them into Status List Tokens as defined in the IETF Token Status List draft-21;
  • manage the lifecycle and revocation of its Digital Credentials and reflect each status change in the applicable Status List without undue delay.

docs.title: 6.6 Provider of Sign/Seal Certificate Requirements
docs.text:
A Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates conforming to this RFC SHALL:

  • issue and manage Sign/Seal Certificates in accordance with the applicable EUDI Wallet certificate profiles;
  • ensure that an OCSP responder is available for every revocable certificate in each Sign/Seal certificate path;
  • include an id-ad-ocsp access location in the Authority Information Access extension of each certificate for which the Provider is responsible;
  • generate OCSP responses conforming to OCSP response, including the required freshness and nonce-processing rules;
  • not use noRevAvail or ext-etsi-valassured-ST-certs to avoid the mandatory OCSP check for Sign/Seal certificate chains;
  • ensure that revocation of a Sign/Seal certificate or a revocable certificate in its certification path is reflected by the mandatory OCSP service without undue delay.

Note: A Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates MAY additionally expose CRL endpoints. A CRL SHALL be treated as supplementary for Sign/Seal certificate chains and SHALL NOT replace the mandatory OCSP track.

docs.title: 7. Interface Definitions
docs.text: This section defines the logical interfaces for conformance testing. The following interfaces are added on top of these added in RFC001, RFC002.

docs.title: 7.1 CRL Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to Provider of WRPAC's CRL endpoint.
  • Method: GET

This endpoint is used for CRL-based X.509 chain revocation checking of WRPAC certificate chains.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
The Wallet SHALL construct an HTTP GET request to retrieve the CRL associated with the certificate being checked in the WRPAC certificate chain.

  • URI Construction:

  • The request URI is extracted directly from the cRLDistributionPoints extension of the certificate.

  • No additional query parameters are required unless explicitly specified by the URI in the CDP extension.

  • Headers:

  • Host: SHALL contain the hostname from the CRL URI.

  • Accept: SHALL contain the value application/pkix-crl.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The Provider's CRL endpoint SHALL respond with the appropriate HTTP status codes and the correctly formatted CRL file if the request is successful.

  • Status Codes:

  • 200 OK: The request was successful, and the CRL is included in the response body.

  • 4xx / 5xx: Standard HTTP error codes (e.g., 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error) SHALL be used only if the server cannot process the HTTP request at the transport level.

  • Headers:

  • Content-Type: SHALL be set to application/pkix-crl for successful responses containing the CRL.

  • Content-Length: SHOULD be included to indicate the size of the CRL file in bytes.

  • Body:

  • The response body SHALL contain the CRL in ASN.1 DER format as specified in RFC 5270.

docs.title: 7.2 OCSP Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to the OCSP responder identified for the certificate being checked.
  • Method: POST

This endpoint is mandatory for X.509 chain revocation checking of Sign/Seal certificate chains. It is optional for WRPAC certificate chains and is used when a WRPAC Provider exposes the optional OCSP track. The Wallet SHALL perform OCSP checking for each revocable certificate in a Sign/Seal certificate chain and MAY perform it for WRPAC certificate chains.

[OPTIONAL] If the DER encoding of the request is less than 255 bytes, the Wallet MAY use the GET method as defined in RFC 6960, by encoding the OCSP request in the URL. In this case, the interface is defined as follows:

  • Direction: Wallet to the OCSP responder
  • Method: GET

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
As detailed in OCSP request, the OCSP request is a DER encoded OCSPRequest structure, with the following parameters:

  • version;

  • requestList with a list of Request structures, each containing:

  • reqCert with the CertID of the certificate to be checked;

  • requestExtensions with the id-pkix-ocsp-nonce extension containing a fresh nonce value.

The Wallet SHALL construct an HTTP POST request to the URI extracted from the Authority Information Access extension of the certificate being checked, specifically the accessLocation associated with the id-ad-ocsp access method.

  • POST Headers: The request SHALL include a Content-Type header set to application/ocsp-request and an Accept header set to application/ocsp-response.
  • POST Body: The body of the POST request SHALL contain the binary DER-encoded OCSPRequest structure.
  • GET Construction (Optional): If utilizing the optional GET method, the request URI SHALL be constructed by appending a URL-encoded Base64 representation of the DER-encoded OCSPRequest to the base OCSP URI (e.g., {OCSP_URI}/{base64_encoded_request}). The GET request SHALL include an Accept header set to application/ocsp-response and has no message body.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
As detailed in OCSP response, the OCSP response is a DER encoded OCSPResponse structure, with the following parameters:

  • responseStatus with the status of the response;

  • responseBytes with the responseType and the response containing the DER encoded BasicOCSPResponse structure, which includes:

  • tbsResponseData with the list of SingleResponse structures, each containing:

    • certID matching the request;
    • certStatus with the status of the certificate (good, revoked, or unknown);
    • thisUpdate and optionally nextUpdate for temporal validity checks.

  • signatureAlgorithm and signatureValue for cryptographic validation;

  • responseExtensions with the id-pkix-ocsp-nonce extension containing the same nonce value as in the request.

If the request is successful, the OCSP responder SHALL respond with the appropriate HTTP status codes and the correctly formatted OCSP response:

  • Status Codes:

  • 200 OK: The request was successfully received and processed. Note that a 200 OK HTTP status SHALL be returned even if the internal OCSP responseStatus indicates an error (e.g., malformedRequest, internalError, tryLater), provided the HTTP transport layer itself succeeded.

  • 4xx / 5xx: Standard HTTP error codes (e.g., 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error) SHALL be used only if the server cannot process the HTTP request at the transport level.

  • Headers:

  • Content-Type: SHALL be set to application/ocsp-response.

  • Content-Length: SHALL accurately reflect the size of the DER-encoded OCSP response in bytes.

  • Cache-Control / Expires: MAY be included to govern HTTP caching behaviors, in case it SHALL align with the nextUpdate field provided in the internal payload.

  • Body Format:

  • The HTTP response body SHALL contain the binary DER-encoded OCSPResponse structure.

docs.title: 7.3 TSL Endpoint
docs.text:
• Direction: Wallet to the applicable Status Provider
  • Method: GET

This endpoint is used for Status List Token validation of WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, and Digital Credentials.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
The Wallet SHALL construct an HTTP GET request to retrieve the Status List Token.

  • URI Construction:

  • The request URI SHALL be extracted from the applicable Status List reference of the token or credential being verified. The reference location and syntax SHALL be determined according to the applicable profile in Section 10.1.

  • Headers:

  • Host: SHALL contain the hostname extracted from the Status List URI.

  • Accept: SHOULD include application/statuslist+jwt and/or application/statuslist+cwt to indicate the Wallet's supported Status List Token representations.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The Status Provider's endpoint SHALL respond with the appropriate HTTP status codes and the correctly formatted Status List Token.

  • Status Codes:

  • 200 OK: The request was successful, and the Status List Token is included in the response body.

  • 4xx / 5xx: Standard HTTP error codes (e.g., 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error) SHALL be used only if the server cannot process the HTTP request at the transport level.

  • Headers:

  • Content-Type: SHALL be set to application/statuslist+jwt for a JWT SLT or application/statuslist+cwt for a CWT SLT.

  • Body:

  • The response body SHALL consist of a JWT or CWT Status List Token.

  • The Status List Token SHALL contain the claims defined in Status List Token.

docs.title: 8.1 Privacy Considerations
docs.text:
While WRPACs, WRPRCs, WIAs, KAs, Digital Credentials, and Sign/Seal Certificates identify organizational entities or Wallet components and need not contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII), the act of validating these artifacts has significant privacy implications for the end-user operating the Wallet.

  • When a Wallet executes a live OCSP request for a certificate in a WRPAC or Sign/Seal certificate chain, the serial number of that certificate is transmitted over the network. A network observer can correlate the OCSP request with the relevant organization, revealing the user's interactions.
  • To obscure the specific endpoints being queried and the parameters of the request, Wallets SHOULD mandate the use of HTTPS (TLS) for all CRL, OCSP, and TSL network queries, despite the payloads already being cryptographically signed.
  • For WRPAC chains, implementers concerned with high-privacy environments SHOULD favor the use of cached CRLs over real-time OCSP queries. By downloading a batched list of statuses, the Wallet obfuscates the specific certificate it is actively verifying, blending the user's specific query into a larger cryptographic dataset. This recommendation does not replace the mandatory OCSP check for Sign/Seal certificate chains.
  • To prevent Wallet Providers from tracking or profiling Users based on their use of Wallet Unit Attestations, Wallet Providers MUST integrate the status information for many WIAs or KAs into the same Status List and MUST publish the SLT at the same uri for all those attestations. Wallet Providers MUST configure Status Lists with at least 100,000 status entries. If more attestations are issued, the Wallet Provider MAY create additional SLTs or increase the number of entries in the array, depending on practical considerations such as the total size of each SLT and the management of multiple endpoints.
  • To prevent Attestation Providers from tracking or profiling Users based on their use of Digital Credentials, Attestation Providers MUST integrate the status information for many PID, QEAA, EAA, or PuB-EAA Digital Credentials into the same Status List and MUST publish the SLT at the same uri for all those attestations. Attestation Providers MUST configure Status Lists with at least 100,000 status entries. If more Digital Credentials are issued, the Attestation Provider MAY create additional SLTs or increase the number of entries in the array, depending on practical considerations such as the total size of each SLT and the management of multiple endpoints.

docs.title: 8.2 Security Considerations
docs.text: Implementations of this specification SHALL account for multiple attack vectors against the PKI and revocation infrastructure. The following considerations establish the baseline security posture for Wallets and Providers of certificates.

docs.title: 8.1.1 Cryptographic Integrity and Trust Anchors
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL NOT rely on deprecated cryptographic algorithms (e.g., SHA-1, RSA-1024) for the signature generation or validation of CRLs, OCSP responses, or Status List Tokens (SLTs).

For X.509 chain revocation checking, Wallets SHALL thoroughly validate the certification path of the OCSP responder or CRL issuer up to a trusted root, verifying that the signer is explicitly authorized to issue revocation data for the certificate being checked (e.g., checking the cRLSign bit or id-kp-OCSPSigning Extended Key Usage).

docs.title: 8.1.2 Freshness and Replay Attacks
docs.text:
To prevent attackers from capturing a valid good OCSP response and replaying it after a certificate has been revoked, Wallets SHALL include the id-pkix-ocsp-nonce in requests and strictly enforce its matching presence in the response.

Wallets SHALL strictly validate the thisUpdate, nextUpdate, iat, and exp fields across all tracks. Systems SHOULD account for minor acceptable clock skew between the Provider and the Wallet, but SHALL reject responses where temporal validity has unambiguously expired, as these may indicate a downgrade or replay attack.

docs.title: 8.1.3 Denial of Service (DoS)
docs.text: Providers of WRPAC and WRPRC, Wallet Providers, and Attestation Providers SHALL ensure high availability of each CRL, OCSP, or TSL endpoint they expose. Providers of Sign/Seal Certificates SHALL ensure high availability of the OCSP responders required for Sign/Seal certificate chains. WRPAC Providers that expose the optional OCSP track SHALL ensure high availability of their OCSP endpoint. Wallets SHALL define a clear policy on how to behave if the revocation endpoint is unreachable (i.e., whether to trust the entity, or abort the transaction).

docs.title: 8.1.4 Transport Security
docs.text: While the integrity of CRLs, OCSP responses, and TSLs is guaranteed by their digital signatures rather than the transport layer, the use of plain HTTP exposes the connection to manipulation. Attackers could intercept requests and return TCP RST packets or spoof 404 Not Found or 500 Internal Server Error responses, forcing the Wallet into a fail-open or fail-closed state without ever evaluating the cryptographic payload.

docs.title: 9. Conformance
docs.text:
An implementation conforms to this specification as a Wallet if it:

  1. implements the requirements defined in Section 6.1;
  2. supports the interfaces defined in Section 7 for CRL-based WRPAC chain checking, OCSP-based Sign/Seal chain checking, and the TSL track;
  3. if it claims support for the optional OCSP track for WRPAC chains, supports the corresponding OCSP interfaces defined in Section 7;
  4. successfully passes all conformance checks defined in the Conformance Check Catalogue for the mandatory tracks and any optional WRPAC OCSP track it claims.

An implementation conforms to this specification as a Provider of WRPAC if it:

  1. implements the requirements defined in Section 6.2;
  2. supports the mandatory CRL interface defined in Section 7;
  3. if it exposes the optional OCSP track for WRPAC chains, supports the corresponding OCSP interface defined in Section 7;

An implementation conforms to this specification as a Provider of WRPRC if it:

  1. implements the requirements defined in Section 6.3;
  2. supports the interfaces defined in Section 7 for the TSL track;

An implementation conforms to this specification as a Wallet Provider if it:

  1. implements the requirements defined in Section 6.4;
  2. supports the TSL interface defined in Section 7 for WIAs and KAs;

An implementation conforms to this specification as an Attestation Provider if it:

  1. implements the requirements defined in Section 6.5;
  2. supports the TSL interface defined in Section 7 for PID, QEAA, EAA, and PuB-EAA Digital Credentials;

An implementation conforms to this specification as a Provider of Sign/Seal Certificates if it:

  1. implements the requirements defined in Section 6.6;
  2. supports the mandatory OCSP interface defined in Section 7 for every revocable certificate in its Sign/Seal certificate paths.

docs.title: 10. Conformance Catalogue and Deployed Test Matrix
10.1 Conformance Check Catalogue
docs.text:
This catalogue defines the baseline conformance checks that support RFC interoperability claims under Section 9. These checks map directly to the normative requirements defined in Sections 6 and 7.

The CRL checks apply to WRPAC certificate chains, the TSL checks apply to WRPRC, WIA, KA, and Digital Credential status, and the OCSP checks apply mandatorily to Sign/Seal certificate chains. OCSP checks for WRPAC certificate chains apply only to implementations that claim support for the optional WRPAC OCSP track.

docs.title: 10.1.1 Token Status List (Wallet Unit Attestation Profile)
docs.text:
This section profiles the Token Status List (TSL) mechanism of the IETF Token Status List draft-21 for Wallet Unit Attestations. A TSL conveys the current status of many Wallet Unit Attestations in a compact, signed Status List Token (SLT).

The SLT Provider MUST be the Wallet Provider.

Status List

A Status List contains a compressed byte array whose entries represent the statuses of many Wallet Instance Attestations (WIAs) or Key Attestations (KAs). A WIA MUST include its Status List reference in client_status.status.status_list, and a KA MUST include its Status List reference in key_storage_status.status.status_list. Each Status List reference MUST contain idx and uri. Both WIAs and KAs are JWTs; therefore, idx is a JSON integer and uri is a JSON string in each reference. In both cases, uri MUST be a URI conforming to RFC 3986.

According to this specification, a WIA or KA can have one of the following statuses:

  • VALID. The WIA or KA is valid. This status is represented by 0x00 in the SLT.
  • INVALID. The WIA or KA is revoked. This status is represented by 0x01 in the SLT.

As a result, the Wallet Provider MUST set the bits parameter in the SLT's status_list object to 1.

The Wallet Provider MUST pack entries starting with the least significant bit of each byte, compress the byte array using DEFLATE with the ZLIB data format, and publish the resulting Status List in the SLT.

Status List Token

The Wallet Provider MUST act as both the Status Issuer and the Status Provider. It MUST make each SLT available via HTTP GET at the URI specified by either the WIA's client_status.status.status_list.uri member or the KA's key_storage_status.status.status_list.uri member, using application/statuslist+jwt for a JWT SLT or application/statuslist+cwt for a CWT SLT.

The SLT format MAY be either a JWT or a CWT and MUST be protected by a cryptographic signature. Regardless of the chosen format, the SLT MUST conform to Section 5.1 for JWTs or Section 5.2 for CWTs of the IETF Token Status List draft-21.

Regardless of the format, the Wallet Provider MUST sign the SLT using one of the following:

  • a valid X.509 certificate whose trust chain terminates at the Trust Anchor published in the Wallet Provider's LoTE when it is registered in the EUDIW Trust Framework; or
  • a valid key attested by the Wallet Provider's Entity Configuration when it is registered in the National Trust Framework.

docs.title: 10.1.2 Token Status List (Digital Credentials Profile)
docs.text:
This section profiles the Token Status List (TSL) mechanism of the IETF Token Status List draft-21 for Digital Credentials. A TSL conveys the current status of many Digital Credentials in a compact, signed Status List Token (SLT).

The SLT Provider MUST be the Credential Issuer, i.e. the applicable Attestation Provider issuing the Digital Credential.

Status List

A Status List contains a compressed byte array whose entries represent the statuses of many Digital Credentials. The Credential Issuer MUST allocate each issued Digital Credential a distinct, non-negative idx value and include it, together with the SLT uri, in the Digital Credential's Status List reference. For an SD-JWT Digital Credential, the reference is in status.status_list, idx is a JSON integer, and uri is a JSON string. For an mdoc MSO, the reference is in issuerAuth.status_list, idx is a CBOR unsigned integer, and uri is a CBOR text string. In both cases, uri MUST be a URI conforming to RFC 3986.

According to this specification, a Digital Credential can have one of the following statuses:

  • VALID. The Digital Credential is valid. This status is represented by 0x00 in the SLT.
  • INVALID. The Digital Credential is revoked. This status is represented by 0x01 in the SLT.
  • SUSPENDED. The Digital Credential is temporarily invalid and may be restored to VALID. This status is represented by 0x02 in the SLT.

As a result, the Credential Issuer MUST set the bits parameter in the SLT's status_list object to 2.

The Credential Issuer MAY define additional application-specific statuses within the range supported by bits. It SHOULD carefully consider the information disclosed to Relying Parties when defining additional statuses for the Digital Credential lifecycle.

The Credential Issuer MUST pack entries starting with the least significant bit of each byte, compress the byte array using DEFLATE with the ZLIB data format, and publish the resulting Status List in the SLT.

Status List Token

The Credential Issuer MUST act as both the Status Issuer and the Status Provider. It MUST make each SLT available via HTTP GET at the URI specified by the Digital Credential's Status List reference, using application/statuslist+jwt for a JWT SLT or application/statuslist+cwt for a CWT SLT.

The SLT format MAY be either a JWT or a CWT and MUST be protected by a cryptographic signature. Regardless of the chosen format, the SLT MUST conform to Section 5.1 for JWTs or Section 5.2 for CWTs of the IETF Token Status List draft-21.

Regardless of the format, the Credential Issuer MUST sign the SLT using one of the following:

  • a valid X.509 certificate whose trust chain terminates at the Trust Anchor published in the Attestation Provider's LoTE when it is registered in the EUDIW Trust Framework; or
  • a valid key attested by the Attestation Provider's Entity Configuration when it is registered in the National Trust Framework.

docs.title: 10.1.3 Common conformance checks
docs.text: Check ID Conformance Check What Is Verified At Runtime Reference CHK-CRL-01 CRL URI Extraction & Method (WRPAC chain) The Wallet extracts the URI from the cRLDistributionPoints extension and executes an HTTP GET request for the WRPAC certificate chain. Sec 7.1 & RFC 5280 CHK-CRL-02 CRL Request Headers The Wallet request contains the Host header and an Accept header strictly set to application/pkix-crl. Sec 7.1 & RFC 5280 CHK-CRL-03 CRL Response Envelope The Provider returns a 200 OK status code with a Content-Type header set to application/pkix-crl. Sec 7.1 & RFC 5280 CHK-CRL-04 CRL Body Format The response body strictly contains an ASN.1 DER formatted CRL. Sec 7.1 & RFC 5280 CHK-CRL-05 CRL Parsing & Validation (WRPAC chain) The Wallet successfully parses and validates the CRL according to RFC 5280. RFC 5280 & APTITUDE Trust Specifications CHK-OCSP-01 OCSP URI Extraction & Method (Sign/Seal mandatory; WRPAC optional) The Wallet extracts the URI from the AIA id-ad-ocsp extension and executes an HTTP POST request for the certificate being checked. Sec 7.2 & RFC 6960 CHK-OCSP-02 OCSP Request Headers & Body The Wallet POST request includes Content-Type: application/ocsp-request, Accept: application/ocsp-response, and a DER-encoded OCSPRequest body. Sec 7.2 & RFC 6960 CHK-OCSP-03 [OPTIONAL] OCSP Request (GET Variant) If the DER request is \(< 255\) bytes and GET is used, the Wallet appends a Base64-encoded OCSPRequest to the URI and omits the body. Sec 7.2 & RFC 6960 CHK-OCSP-04 OCSP Response Envelope The Provider returns a 200 OK status code (even for internal OCSP errors) with Content-Type: application/ocsp-response. Sec 7.2 & RFC 6960 CHK-OCSP-05 OCSP Body Format & Parsing (Sign/Seal mandatory; WRPAC optional) The Provider returns a binary DER-encoded OCSPResponse, and the Wallet supports parsing/validation for the certificate being checked. Sec 7.2, RFC 6960 & APTITUDE Trust Specifications CHK-TSL-01 TSL Reference Extraction & Method The Wallet extracts the Status List URI and index from the artifact-specific Status List reference and executes an HTTP GET request. Sec 7.3 & Section 10.1 CHK-TSL-02 TSL Request Headers The Wallet request includes the Host header and SHOULD include Accept values for the JWT and/or CWT SLT representations it supports. Sec 7.3 & TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-03 TSL Response Envelope The Status Provider returns 200 OK with application/statuslist+jwt or application/statuslist+cwt, consistent with the returned SLT format. Sec 7.3 & TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-04 TSL Body Format The response body strictly contains a JWT or CWT Status List Token. Sec 7.3 & TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-05 Referenced Artifact Pre-check The Wallet validates the referenced artifact before using its Status List reference. Section 6.1 & applicable artifact profile CHK-TSL-06 Status List Reference Syntax The Wallet validates the presence, type, URI syntax, and non-negative integer encoding of idx and uri as required by the applicable profile. Section 10.1.1 and Section 10.1.2 CHK-TSL-07 SLT Integrity The Wallet verifies the SLT signature using a trusted and authorized key. TSL Draft-21 & applicable profile CHK-TSL-08 SLT Subject Binding The Wallet verifies that the SLT subject identifies the URI in the referenced artifact's Status List reference. TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-09 SLT Temporal Validity The Wallet verifies the applicable iat, exp, and ttl claims against current_time. TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-10 SLT Parsing & Decompression The Wallet decompresses the lst claim using DEFLATE with the ZLIB data format. TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-11 Index Boundary Check The Wallet verifies that the artifact's idx is within the bounds of the decompressed Status List. TSL Draft-21 CHK-TSL-12 Status Resolution Dispatch The Wallet reads the entry at idx and applies the status mapping and acceptance decision defined by the applicable artifact profile. Applicable TSL profile

docs.title: 10.1.4 Profile-specific conformance checks
docs.text: Check ID Conformance Check What Is Verified At Runtime Reference CHK-TSL-WUA-01 Wallet Unit Attestation Reference The Wallet checks client_status.status.status_list for a WIA and key_storage_status.status.status_list for a KA, including the required JSON types. Section 10.1.1 CHK-TSL-WUA-02 Wallet Unit Attestation Status Encoding The Wallet Provider's SLT has bits: 1 and maps 0x00 to VALID and 0x01 to INVALID. Section 10.1.1 CHK-TSL-DC-01 Digital Credential Reference The Wallet checks status.status_list for an SD-JWT Digital Credential and issuerAuth.status_list for an mdoc MSO, including the required JSON or CBOR types. Section 10.1.2 CHK-TSL-DC-02 Digital Credential Status Encoding The Wallet checks bits: 2 and maps 0x00 to VALID, 0x01 to INVALID, and 0x02 to SUSPENDED; status values 0x03 and above are not used by this profile. Section 10.1.2

docs.title: 10.2 Deployed Test Case Matrix
docs.text:
The test matrix codes are generated by the three tracks defined in this RFC (CRL, OCSP, TSL). OCSP test cases apply only when the optional OCSP track is claimed. The test case ID is defined as follows:

  • An initial code describing the track (CRL, OCSP, TSL).
  • A second code for the type of checks (REQ for request schema, RES for response schema, VAL for validation checks).
  • An increasing natural number.
Test Case ID Deployed Scenario Request Profile / Variant Checks Covered Expected Outcome CRL-REQ-01 Standard CRL Retrieval HTTP GET via CDP Wallet sends GET request with valid Host and Accept: application/pkix-crl headers. Response returns application/pkix-crl and file is valid ASN.1 DER. CRL-RES-01 Valid CRL Response Provider Successful Serve Provider returns 200 OK, valid Content-Type, and binary DER CRL file. Successful download of the CRL payload. CRL-VAL-01 Freshness Verification Temporal Check Comparison of current_time against thisUpdate and nextUpdate fields. CRL is accepted if thisUpdate ≤ current_time < nextUpdate; otherwise, attempt refresh. CRL-VAL-02 Issuer Identification Direct CRL Matching Comparison of CRL issuer field with the certificate's issuer field (when DP cRLIssuer is omitted). Binary match between Name structures; proceed if identical, otherwise reject CRL. CRL-VAL-03 Indirect CRL Binding cRLIssuer Present Match CRL issuer field with cRLIssuer in DP; verify indirectCRL boolean in IDP is TRUE. Match successful; CRL is used as an authoritative source for non-issuer revocations. CRL-VAL-04 IDP Scope: Distribution Partitioned CRL Match distributionPoint name in CRL IDP extension with the name in the certificate's DP. Exact string match on the URI or Distinguished Name; CRL accepted for that scope. CRL-VAL-05 IDP Scope: Cert Type EE vs. CA Scope Verify onlyContainsUserCerts or onlyContainsCACerts against certificate basicConstraints. Rejection of the CRL if an EE cert is checked against a CA-only CRL (and vice-versa). CRL-VAL-06 Path Integrity Signer Authorization Validation of the CRL issuer's certification path to the same trust anchor as the target certificate. Successful path validation; verification that the CRL signer's certificate has the cRLSign bit set. CRL-VAL-07 Signature Verification Cryptographic Check Validation of the digital signature on the complete CRL using the validated public key of the CRL issuer. Signature is cryptographically valid; CRL data is considered authentic. CRL-VAL-08 Status Resolution Revocation Search Search for the certificate's serial number within the revokedCertificates list. If found, cert_status matches the reason code; if not found, status is VALID. OCSP-REQ-01 Standard OCSP Status Request HTTP POST Wallet sends POST to the AIA URI for a Sign/Seal certificate chain (mandatory) or WRPAC chain (optional) with valid OCSP MIME types and DER body. 200 OK with a valid binary OCSPResponse payload. OCSP-REQ-02 Short OCSP Status Request HTTP GET (Optional) Wallet successfully encodes < 255 byte request as Base64 in URL parameter. 200 OK and successful HTTP caching where applicable. OCSP-RES-01 Valid OCSP Response Provider Successful Serve Provider returns 200 OK (transport level success), valid MIME type, and DER response. Successful download of the OCSP payload. OCSP-VAL-01 Response Type Check Basic Response Type Verification that responseType OID matches id-pkix-ocsp-basic ({1 3 6 1 5 5 7 48 1 1}). Reject if the response is not the basic type; OCSP clients SHALL support this type. OCSP-VAL-02 Cryptographic Integrity Digital Signature Verification of the signature value across the hash of the DER encoded ResponseData. Signature SHALL be valid; reject response if cryptographic check fails. OCSP-VAL-03 Responder Authorization CA Signature Check if the response is signed by the CA that issued the certificate in question. Proceed to status evaluation if the CA signature is verified. OCSP-VAL-04 Responder Authorization Authorized Responder Verification of id-kp-OCSPSigning (OID {1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.9}) in the Extended Key Usage extension of a responder certificate issued directly by the CA. Proceed if Extended Key Usage is present and the signer matches the intended recipient. OCSP-VAL-05 CertID Correlation Request-Response Binding Match the CertID (hashAlgorithm, hashes, serialNumber) in the response to the original request. Reject if the response does not correspond to the requested certificate. OCSP-VAL-06 Temporal Validity Freshness Check Comparison of thisUpdate against local system time to ensure it is "sufficiently recent". Reject if thisUpdate is in the future or considered stale by local policy. OCSP-VAL-07 Temporal Validity nextUpdate Check Verification that current time is less than nextUpdate (if provided). Reject as unreliable if system time is past nextUpdate. OCSP-VAL-08 Status Resolution Final Status Mapping Retrieval of certStatus: good, revoked (with reason/time), or unknown. Target certificate is accepted only if status is good. OCSP-EXT-01 Replay Protection Nonce Validation Verification that the nonce in the response matches the nonce sent in the requestExtensions. Reject response if nonces do not match, preventing replay attacks. TSL-REQ-01 Standard TSL Retrieval HTTP GET via an artifact-specific Status List reference Wallet extracts the URI and index correctly and sends GET request with the required Host header. Status Provider returns 2xx and the raw Status List Token. TSL-RES-01 Valid TSL Response Provider Successful Serve Provider returns 200 OK, a matching JWT or CWT content type, and a Status List Token payload. Successful resolution of the SLT from the endpoint. TSL-VAL-01 Referenced Artifact Pre-check Artifact Validation Wallet validates the referenced WIA, KA, WRPRC, or Digital Credential before checking its status. Proceed to SLT fetching only if the referenced artifact is valid; otherwise reject. TSL-VAL-02 Status List Reference Syntax Profile-specific Reference Wallet validates the applicable reference claims and the idx and uri types and syntax. Validation succeeds if the reference adheres to its artifact profile. TSL-VAL-03 SLT Integrity Cryptographic Validation Signature verification of the SLT (JWT or CWT format) using a trusted and authorized key. Reject SLT if signature is invalid or undetermined. TSL-VAL-04 Subject Binding URI Consistency sub (JWT) or 2 (CWT) claim in SLT identifies the uri in the referenced artifact's Status List reference. Reject SLT if identifiers are not equal. TSL-VAL-05 Temporal Validity Expiration & Freshness Verification of iat, exp, and ttl claims; comparison against current_time. Reject SLT if current time is past exp or the token is otherwise stale. TSL-VAL-06 Parsing & Decompression SLT Content Extraction Decompression of the lst claim using DEFLATE with the ZLIB data format. Successful recovery of the uncompressed Status List. TSL-VAL-07 Index Boundary Check Bit Array Access Verification that the idx from the referenced artifact is within the bounds of the decompressed Status List. Reject the referenced artifact if the index is out of bounds. TSL-VAL-08 Profile-specific Status Resolution Status Type Evaluation Retrieval of the entry at idx and application of the status mapping defined by the applicable profile. Final decision is made according to the applicable artifact profile. TSL-WUA-01 Wallet Unit Attestation Status Resolution bits: 1 Retrieval of the entry at idx and mapping 0x00 to VALID and 0x01 to INVALID. WIA or KA is accepted only when status is VALID. TSL-DC-01 Digital Credential Status Resolution bits: 2 Retrieval of the entry at idx and mapping 0x00 to VALID, 0x01 to INVALID, and 0x02 to SUSPENDED. Digital Credential is accepted only when status is VALID; SUSPENDED is handled according to issuer policy.

docs.title: Testing and Conformance Overview
docs.text:
This section explains how APTITUDE participants validate implementation readiness using ITB+ and how conformance evidence is submitted to WP2/T2.2.

Use the onboarding guide for end-to-end operational steps, screenshots, and report submission details.

  • ITB+ User Onboarding Guide
  • Reporting Conformance Results

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The current ITB+ onboarding and conformance flow supports testing for:

  • Wallet Unit
  • Issuer
  • Verifier

docs.title: Recommended Path
docs.text:
1. Request onboarding access and provide organisation and technical contact details.
  2. Access ITB+ and open the APTITUDE conformance statements area.
  3. Execute relevant test cases for the selected RFC profile and role.
  4. Inspect logs and download conformance reports.
  5. Submit successful conformance evidence to WP2/T2.2.

For complete instructions, follow the full guide:

  • APTITUDE ITB+ User Onboarding Manual

docs.title: APTITUDE ITB+ User Onboarding Manual
docs.text:

Authors: Nikos Triantafyllou & Petros Kavassalis, UAegean i4m Lab Reviewers: Luca Vallone, IPZS.IT; Giancarlo Degani, INFOCERT
